articles.title: Real Or Fake: Are 3-0 Starts For Bills, Chiefs, 49ers, Vikes & Raiders Legit Or Mirage?
articles.summary: If recent history carries into this year, at least one of the five 3-0 teams will miss the playoffs. Which team could it be? We determine which 3-0 starts are real or fake.
articles.body: For five teams in the NFL, the 2026 season couldn't have gotten off to a better start. The Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs, San Francisco 49ers, Las Vegas Raiders and Minnesota Vikings are all 3-0 to start the season. For the Bills and Chiefs, their starts have become what we've grown accustomed to seeing in recent years. And after the 49ers' upset of the Los Angeles Rams in Week 1, it isn't a shock they're 3-0, either. But the Raiders and Vikings have been the biggest surprises so far this year, with each already recording multiple upset victories. And in Las Vegas' case, it's off to a 3-0 start after holding the No. 1 overall pick in this past year's draft. While a 3-0 start is certainly encouraging, it doesn't guarantee a spot in the postseason. In fact, 33 of the 45 teams (73.3%) that started 3-0 over the last 10 years went on to make the playoffs, per FOX Sports Research. Four of the six teams that went 3-0 last season also went on to make the playoffs. So, if recent history carries into this year, at least one of the five 3-0 teams will miss the playoffs in 2026. Which team could it be? We determine which 3-0 starts are real or fake. Buffalo Bills: Real Steven Ruiz: Very real. I know we say this every season, but this might be the best chance the Bills have at getting over the Super Bowl hump. It starts with Josh Allen, because of course it does. It appears he’s leveled up his game. The ball is getting out quicker, and he’s seeing coverages better than he ever has. The Bills offensive line remains strong, and the run game takes playmaking pressure off Allen. The pieces are in place for another MVP-caliber campaign for No. 17. But it’s the defense that really has me thinking this team has a real shot at hoisting the Lombardi Trophy in February. New defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard is installing a scheme that should give quarterbacks more issues compared to Sean McDermott’s static defense. And the emergence of defensive tackle Deone Walker as an interior menace, along with the continued ascension of Greg Rousseau, gives Leonhard a defensive line that will wreck game plans. The ceiling for the offense is as high as ever, and the defense’s ceiling is higher than ever in Buffalo. Kansas City Chiefs: Real Ben Arthur: First of all, Patrick Mahomes is back from the torn ACL and LCL he suffered in December, and he’s off to a great start in 2026 — a 68.4% completion rate for 912 yards and seven touchdowns against just two interceptions with a 108.9 passer rating, plus 10 carries for 41 yards and another score. The two-time MVP should only get more comfortable as the season wears on and he’s further removed from knee surgery. But the biggest reason why the Chiefs are a true Super Bowl contender, and not just in the conversation with a healthy Mahomes, is because of running back Kenneth Walker III. The reigning Super Bowl MVP’s dynamic ability out of the backfield has opened up Kansas City’s offense in a way we haven’t seen in the Mahomes era. For years, we’ve been talking about how the Chiefs haven’t had a consistently dominant and available WR1 since the Tyreek Hill days, but Walker’s presence has allowed the Chiefs’ offense to be explosive without one. The attention he draws brings safeties down to the box, freeing up shots in the pass game. It’s a big reason why we see 37-year-old Travis Kelce (77.0 receiving yards per game) and wide receiver Rashee Rice (63.3) finding so much success. And then, of course, Walker is doing damage when he actually touches the ball. The former Seahawk is leading the league with 360 rushing yards and 34 missed tackles forced (next closest is the Lions’ Jahmyr Gibbs at 22), according to Pro Football Focus. The Chiefs currently rank second in total offense (416.3 yards/game) and tied for seventh in scoring (29.3). They’re also getting it defensively, ranking third in points allowed (16.7) and fourth in yards allowed per game (278.0). Between Mahomes, Walker and the highly effective units around them, Kansas City is absolutely in the Super Bowl conversation. San Francisco 49ers: Real Eric Williams: The 49ers lose key healthy bodies each week, but the same thing happens every year and head coach Kyle Shanahan patches enough holes to make it work. Edge rusher Nick Bosa, linebacker Fred Warner, wide receiver Ricky Pearsall, quarterback Brock Purdy and tight end George Kittle all missed games due to injury last season, but San Francisco still finished in the playoffs at 12-5. This year, Purdy is the frontrunner for MVP and new defensive coordinator Raheem Morris hasn’t missed a beat replacing the departed Robert Saleh. And rookie running back Kaelon Black has been a nice backup for Christian McCaffrey, giving the All-Pro a break at times so he doesn’t break down at the end of the year. The Los Angeles Rams were supposed to be the superteam leading the NFC West, but San Francisco overwhelmed them in Australia to start the year and have proven over the years they can keep it going, despite injuries. Las Vegas Raiders: Fake Greg Auman: It’s cruel to make this a pass/fail. No team in the NFL has overachieved more than the Raiders have to be 3-0. Kirk Cousins has shown why it was smart to let Fernando Mendoza wait, and the defense has been a surprising spark. Linebacker Nakobe Dean has three forced fumbles and looks like a smart signing; rookie corner Hezekiah Masses has three interceptions in the last two games. However, they’re in a division with the 3-0 Chiefs and 2-1 Broncos, and they still have four games against those two. And consider their next four games: vs. Chiefs, at Patriots, vs. Bills, vs. Rams. They could be a really good team and go 0-4 in those games. They will far exceed their preseason projected win total of 5.5 wins, and head coach Klint Kubiak has already changed the culture in a locker room that needed it. I just don’t know that it translates to even a wild card this season. Here’s how to map it out: They have five games left against teams in the bottom 10 of the current FOX Sports Power Rankings: Browns, Jets, Chargers, Cardinals and Titans. Take four of those five and get two surprise wins in the other eight games, and you’re 9-8 and a wild card and one of the best turnarounds in the league, and there’s nothing fake about that. Minnesota Vikings: Real Henry McKenna: Given the value of quarterbacks in this league, it says something when a team is winning without one. The win over the Bears was legit. Kyler Murray has been in and out of the lineup (and back in again). He has played just one complete game, and he hasn’t been spectacular. But that’s sort of the whole point. The idea was to let Murray ride the wave of the offense, starting as a guy who — at the very least — wouldn’t get in the way. (Hate to throw J.J. McCarthy under the bus, but that’s what he couldn’t figure out. His turnovers and outside-the-system decision-making cost him a job.) Murray is right where he needs to be to start the season: a modest system quarterback. He can grow into a role as a facilitator and — then maybe coach Kevin O’Connell will let the training wheels off when everyone is comfortable. Ironically, we’ve spent the last few years talking about O’Connell and his quarterbacks. But it’s Brian Flores who really has this team firing. The Vikings' defense has the second-fewest points per game allowed. They have the most sacks (14), led by edges Dallas Turner (3.5) and Andrew Van Ginkel (3) and linebacker Blake Cashman (2.5). Flores’ game plans are like an escape room for a quarterback. And I haven’t seen a quarterback solve it this year.

articles.title: NFL: Cleveland Browns survive a late comeback to defeat Pittsburgh Steelers
articles.summary: Andre Szmyt kicks a match-winning 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds remaining as the Cleveland Browns survive a Pittsburgh Steelers comeback.
articles.body:
Andre Szmyt kicked a match-winning 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds remaining as the Cleveland Browns survived a Pittsburgh Steelers comeback in a thrilling encounter at Huntington Bank Field.

Szmyt's career-best effort, followed by a late interception by safety Grant Delpit, ensured a 27-24 victory for the Browns, who have now won three consecutive games.

The hosts led 21-10 lead at the end of the third quarter, but divisional rivals Pittsburgh fought back with Aaron Rodgers finding tight end Pat Freiermuth in the endzone before adding a two-point conversion to level the scores with one minute and 42 seconds remaining.

Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson, who was booed by some Browns fans in pre-season, responded by moving his team 36 yards over seven plays to set up Szmyt's winning kick.

The Steelers led 7-0 at the end of the first quarter following a Roman Wilson touchdown, but the Browns enjoyed a dominant second period to lead by 11 at half-time.

Jaleel McLaughlin and Quinshon Judkins rushed into the endzone and Harold Fannin Jr took a scoring catch, while Chris Boswell kicked a field goal for the Steelers.

A scoreless third quarter followed, before a Darnell Washington touchdown for the Steelers closed the gap.

A 44-yard field goal from Szmyt gave the Browns some breathing room, before Rodgers, who was sacked five times and intercepted twice, threw to Freiermuth to start an exhilarating conclusion.

The Browns now lead the AFC North division for the first time since November 2014, while the Steelers sit bottom with a record of two wins and two defeats.

articles.title: NFL Players Who Could Use a Change of Scenery After Steelers Trade Joey Porter Jr. to Cowboys
articles.summary: Late Wednesday evening, the Dallas Cowboys made a move to bolster their secondary by trading for Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr.
articles.body:
Late Wednesday evening, the Dallas Cowboys made a move to bolster their secondary by trading for Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr.

For Porter, the deal means a fresh start and another opportunity to secure a second contract before the 2027 offseason.

The 26-year-old has been seeking a new deal since early in the offseason. Dallas will not give him a new contract upon his arrival, according to Clarence Hill Jr. of DLLS. The Steelers have traditionally declined to negotiate contracts during the regular season, whereas the Cowboys have shown a greater willingness to pay players they view as core pieces.

"Definitely felt disrespected. Definitely felt undervalued," Porter told reporters on Thursday. "But that's old news now."

In that context, the change of venue should benefit Porter greatly. He's not the only NFL veteran who could use greener—or at least different—pastures in 2026.

Here's a look at eight more players who could use a change of scenery, why a move could benefit them and which landing spots might suit them best.

Jerry Jeudy has shown that he can be a very good starting receiver in the past. He had a pair of 800-yard seasons with the Denver Broncos, and he made the Pro Bowl after a 1,229-yard campaign with the Cleveland Browns in 2024.

There was a time when it seemed that Jeudy was firmly in Cleveland's long-term plans, too. The Browns traded for Jeudy in 2024 and immediately signed him to a three-year, $52.5 million extension. Now, though, it feels like another move would be best for the Alabama product.

The Browns used early picks in April's draft on wide receivers KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston . They represent Cleveland's future at receiver and, in many ways, they're already pushing out Jeudy. Through the first four weeks of the season, he has caught just five passes, and he was only targeted once across Weeks 2 and 3.

At only 27 years old, Jeudy still has an opportunity to reestablish himself as a high-end receiver, but he's probably not going to do that in Cleveland. He would benefit greatly from a team that has an established and consistent quarterback, along with a long-term need at wide receiver.

Ideal Landing Spots: Los Angeles Rams, San Francisco 49ers

Marvin Harrison Jr., WR, Arizona Cardinals

Like Jeudy, Marvin Harrison Jr. is a first-round pick who has never quite played up to his draft status for the team that selected him.

The Arizona Cardinals took the Ohio State product fourth overall in 2024, and while he had a strong rookie season (885 yards, 8 TDs), he has regressed since.

Harrison has also watched as fellow receiver Michael Wilson has become Arizona's top perimeter target. Through Week 3, Harrison had caught just four of nine targets for 73 yards.

According to ESPN's Dan Graziano , executives around the league are wondering if the Cardinals could make the 24-year-old available. According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , though, he might only command a high Day 3 pick in a trade.

Arizona probably won't want to move Harrison at that price point, but he should relish the prospect of a fresh start.

Unless something changes dramatically, Harrison risks being labeled a disappointment for as long as he remains with the Cardinals. He's not going to establish himself as a true No. 1 receiver in Arizona either.

Landing with a team that lacks a true top option could be Harrison's best bet for reestablishing his NFL stock.

Ideal Landing Spots: Las Vegas Raiders, Pittsburgh Steelers

The Dallas Cowboys have made several trades over the past calendar year, and they haven't been all about acquiring talent. They cashed in 2023 first-round pick Mazi Smith as part of their bid for Quinnen Williams.

Unfortunately, Smith isn't the only early 2023 draft pick who has disappointed the Cowboys. Second-round pick Luke Schoonmaker has appeared in 15 more games in Dallas than Smith did, but he hasn't made much of an offensive impact.

Schoonmaker has caught just 51 passes for 459 yards and three touchdowns, and he's now firmly cemented behind starting tight end Jake Ferguson. He's played just 24 percent of the offensive snaps this season.

Now in the final year of his rookie deal, Schoonmaker is unlikely to establish himself as a starter in Dallas, and he's not going to earn a lucrative free-agent contract with modest numbers. He would benefit from joining a team that either lacks a No. 1 receiving tight end or has lost one to injury.

Ideal Landing Spots: Miami Dolphins, Philadelphia Eagles

NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 4 🏈

In 2024, the Carolina Panthers traded up to take wide receiver Xavier Legette with the last pick in the first round. He was expected to become a go-to target for quarterback Bryce Young, but he's been anything but an impact receiver.

Legette recorded just 49 catches for 497 yards and four touchdowns as a rookie. The following offseason, the Panthers used a first-round pick on Tetairoa McMillan, who quickly became the No. 1 option that Legette wasn't.

The South Carolina product had just 363 yards and three touchdowns in his second season, and he had just two catches through the first two weeks of 2026. Legette is currently dealing with a knee injury and missed Week 3, but he simply hasn't been a big part of the offense since McMillan arrived and Jalen Coker emerged as the No. 2 option.

Legette may simply not be cut out to be a true No. 1 receiver, but he could still establish himself as a high-end complementary target. He should hope to land with a potent passing offense that would make use of his 4.39 speed, 6'1", 220-pound frame, and physical playing style.

Ideal Landing Spots: Kansas City Chiefs, Philadelphia Eagles

Anthony Richardson, QB, Indianapolis Colts

Porter isn't the only player who got a new opportunity this week. On Monday, the Minnesota Vikings dealt quarterback and 2024 first-round pick J.J. McCarthy to the New York Giants.

According to Fowler , the Giants did not inquire about Indianapolis Colts backup Anthony Richardson before acquiring McCarthy.

Fowler also reported that the Colts are not particularly interested in moving Richardson, although a chance to play in a Kyle Shanahan- or Sean McVay-style offense could appeal to the quarterback.

The 2023 first-round pick entered his third NFL season behind Daniel Jones on the Indianapolis depth chart. However, the 24-year-old still possesses considerable physical upside and has time to get his career back on track.

However, Richardson is unlikely to draw significant interest as a prospective starter in 2027 free agency. Landing with a team facing uncertainty at quarterback next offseason could give him a chance to reestablish himself and compete for a starting job.

Ideal Landing Spots: Miami Dolphins, Minnesota Vikings

Felix Anudike-Uzomah, Edge, Kansas City Chiefs

With the Kansas City Chiefs sitting at 3-0 and looking a lot like the perennial contenders they've been for the better part of a decade, there probably aren't many players eager to leave the franchise. However, Felix Anudike-Uzomah should be interested in finding a team that can give him a better opportunity.

The 24-year-old was the 31st overall pick in the 2023 draft, but he's never made much of an impact in Kansas City. He played less than a third of the defensive snaps in each of his first two seasons, missed all of 2025 with a hamstring injury, and had his fifth-year option declined by the Chiefs.

While the Kansas State product has started all three games this season, he has played just 47 percent of the defensive snaps and has logged just two tackles and a sack. It seems like only a matter of time before rookie second-round pick R Mason Thomas becomes the primary complement to George Karlaftis on the edge.

Anudike-Uzomah would be well-served to land with another playoff-caliber team that can give him a prominent rotational role and a clearer path to a long-term role than he'll find in Kansas City.

Ideal Landing Spots: Baltimore Ravens, Chicago Bears

Unlike the Chiefs, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers are not playing like 2026 contenders. They remain winless entering Week 4 and just lost starting quarterback Baker Mayfield to a dislocated thumb for the next few weeks .

The Buccaneers' situation feels a lot different than it did just before the start of the season when Vita Vea agreed to a one-year, $30 million contract extension. That agreement came weeks after the defensive tackle requested a trade, citing his lack of a new contract.

While the 2018 No. 12 overall pick is under contract through 2027, there's no guarantee he'll play out his contract in Tampa. The Bucs could save $11 million in cap space by trading him in the spring or $24 million by trading him after June 1. That could be a real possibility if the team continues to flounder and looks to rebuild in the offseason.

With the Buccaneers' season trending in the wrong direction, Vea could welcome an opportunity to join a playoff contender. He will turn 32 in February, but he remains a top-tier interior defender who could help a team pursuing a Super Bowl.

Ideal Landing Spots: Buffalo Bills, San Francisco 49ers

Brian Thomas Jr., WR, Jacksonville Jaguars

Brian Thomas Jr. was spectacular as a rookie for the Jacksonville Jaguars, racking up 1,282 yards and making the Pro Bowl in 2024. However, he has been far less productive in the team's offense since head coach Liam Coen took over in 2025.

Thomas had just 48 catches for 707 yards and two touchdowns last season. This year, he's become even less involved while watching Parker Washington establish himself as Jacksonville's WR1.

With Thomas sliding into the WR3 role behind Washington and Jakobi Meyers, the 23-year-old may want a fresh start somewhere else. The 2-1 Jags may prefer to keep him for their 2026 run, of course, but that hasn't put an end to the trade speculation.

Bleacher Report's Alex Kay recently examined five landing spots that could help rejuvenate Thomas' career.

While most receiver-needy teams could benefit from adding Thomas, he should be looking to land with a team that lacks a clear No. 1 wideout. Finding one that can also make a playoff run this season would be a bonus.

Ideal Landing Spots: Las Vegas Raiders, San Francisco 49ers

articles.title: Pro Bowl Safety Emerges as Intriguing Lions Trade Target
articles.summary: Falcons safety Jessie Bates II has been identified as an intriguing Detroit Lions trade target as Brad Holmes continues searching for secondary help.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions already showed they were willing to investigate a significant addition to their secondary when they explored a trade for Joey Porter Jr. Now another name has surfaced who would represent an entirely different kind of swing.

Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III has been identified as an intriguing potential target for Detroit before the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline. This is not a report that the Falcons are shopping Bates or that Brad Holmes has called Atlanta, but the fit is fascinating enough to deserve a closer look.

Jessie Bates III Named Potential Lions Trade Target

Morgan Cannon and Anthony Balaj included Bates among nine defensive backs the Lions could consider after Dallas beat Detroit to Porter. Their reasoning centers on Detroit's immediate need at safety and Bates entering the final year of his contract with Atlanta.

Bates would not be another temporary body added simply to survive an injury crisis. The 29-year-old has been one of the NFL's most productive safeties for years, recording 27 career interceptions and 71 passes defended while starting every game he has played since entering the league in 2018.

His three seasons in Atlanta have been particularly impressive. Bates intercepted 13 passes from 2023-25, including six during his first year with the Falcons, while producing at least 97 tackles in each of those three seasons.

There is an important complication, however. Bates said during the offseason that he wants to retire with Atlanta , even though he acknowledged that the Falcons had not approached him about a contract extension at that point.

Detroit's interest in upgrading the secondary is no longer theoretical. The Lions investigated Porter before Pittsburgh ultimately traded him to Dallas, and they have since been connected to several other possible cornerback targets .

Bates would address a different problem. Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph opened the season on the PUP list, Avonte Maddox has already been lost for the year , and Detroit has been forced to lean heavily on veterans Chuck Clark and Christian Izien.

Branch and Joseph can become eligible to return, but eligibility does not guarantee availability. Dan Campbell has already made it clear that Detroit will not rush Joseph back before his knee is ready.

Adding Bates would immediately give Kelvin Sheppard another proven playmaker in the back end of his defense. It would also create the possibility of eventually pairing Bates with Branch, giving Detroit two versatile defensive backs capable of disguising coverages and making plays on the football.

There are obvious reasons a Bates trade would be difficult. Atlanta would first have to decide it is willing to move one of its best defensive players, and the Falcons have given no public indication that they are ready to do that.

Then there is the contract situation. Bates is scheduled to reach free agency after this season, meaning Detroit would have to decide whether it views him as an expensive rental or someone worth extending beyond 2026.

That could actually be part of the appeal if Atlanta falls out of contention. Rather than losing Bates in free agency, the Falcons could theoretically decide that recovering draft capital makes more sense if the two sides are not headed toward another contract.

For Detroit, everything would come down to acquisition cost. Holmes has generally resisted sacrificing premium future assets for short-term fixes, but the Lions' pursuit of Porter showed that he is at least willing to examine significant defensive upgrades.

The Lions don't need another name simply because the trade deadline is approaching. They need someone capable of changing a defense that has already been stretched thin in the secondary.

If Atlanta ever decides Jessie Bates III is actually available, Holmes should have a very interesting phone call to make.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers’ relationship timeline reveals his journey from high-profile romances with celebrities to a secretive marriage with Brittani
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers has moved from dating actresses and a racing star to keeping his marriage almost completely private.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers has moved from dating actresses and a racing star to keeping his marriage almost completely private. The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback married a woman named Brittani in 2025, and the couple has shared very little since. In his Netflix docuseries "Aaron Rodgers: Enigma," Rodgers said he "despised" the attention that came with dating women who were already famous. His past includes Olivia Munn, Danica Patrick and Shailene Woodley. Here is how the timeline unfolded, from his first reported romance in 2011 to what he said about his wife in September.What does Aaron Rodgers' relationship timeline show about his shift from celebrity romances to a private marriage?The pattern is hard to miss. For more than a decade, Rodgers dated women with public profiles, and cameras followed most of those relationships. His marriage looks like a deliberate reset.Brittani does not use social media, and when Rodgers first mentioned her in December 2024, he only revealed that her name is spelled "Brittani with an 'i'." He called her his girlfriend while talking about a Christmas package on The Pat McAfee Show, almost as an aside. By June 2025, he confirmed they were married and said the wedding had happened a couple of months earlier. That is a sharp turn for a man whose earlier relationships played out on red carpets.Who are the famous women Aaron Rodgers has dated?Jessica Szohr came first in 2011. The Gossip Girl actress and Rodgers reportedly reconnected a few years later, and she attended his 2017 birthday celebration. They never made it official.Olivia Munn was the longest of his public relationships. They met at the 2014 ACM Awards while presenting an award together, and Munn joked that she did not even know who he was at first. Rodgers once said he was "real happy" with her. After three years, they split in 2017.Kelly Rohrbach, a Sports Illustrated model, is a smaller footnote. Golf photos in 2017 sparked rumors, but a source said they were only friends.Danica Patrick followed in 2018. The two met at the 2012 ESPYs. Rodgers said they were "really into each other," and they bought a Malibu home in 2019 before splitting in 2020.Shailene Woodley brought the biggest surprise. Rodgers revealed their engagement during his NFL MVP acceptance speech in 2021, and Woodley confirmed it later on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon. Rodgers called it "the best thing that's happened" to him. They split in 2022 as careers and distance got in the way. Mallory Edens, a model and the daughter of the Milwaukee Bucks owner, was linked to him in early 2023, but it did not last long.What has Aaron Rodgers said about his wife Brittani?On Sept. 10, 2026, Rodgers appeared on "Not Just Football with Cam Heyward" and opened up more about her."In 2017 I met my wife, and at the time, she was leaving the States and going back to Europe," he said in the interview. "My biggest regret is not begging her to stay or proposing right there, because that sent me right there into a tailspin of what can I be accused of as a partner in a relationship."The timing stands out. Rodgers and Munn split in 2017, the same year he says he met his wife. articles.title: ‘Taken a step back’ – 2X Super Bowl champion calls out Justin Herbert after his poor performances for the LA Chargers
articles.summary: Two-time Super Bowl champion LeSean McCoy has called out the LA Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert after his poor start to the season despite being given al...
articles.body:
Two-time Super Bowl champion LeSean McCoy has called out the LA Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert after his poor start to the season despite being given all the resources.

In three games, the 28-year-old has thrown for 627 yards and has four interceptions to his name, which is the second most in the league behind Drake Maye.

A lot was expected from the Chargers and Herbert going into this season, but with the 0-3 start, they once again look like a team that will crash out without making the playoffs. What makes it harder for the Chargers is that they have a tough schedule coming up.

Throughout the three games, one person who has come under the most scrutiny has been their star, QB Justin Herbert. With the team preparing to play the Seattle Seahawks next, LeSean McCoy has also added to the list of analysts and former players who have expressed their disappointment on his poor form this season.

McCoy believes despite having it all Herbert has taken a step back

Before the start of the season, many analysts had Herbert and the Chargers as the player and team to watch out for. However, they have been extremely disappointing since Week 1, and their next test is going to be even harder, as it is the defending champions who await them.

Herbert, who now has a new offensive coordinator, is completing only 59.1% of his passes, which has been a huge 'step back' according to McCoy.

"You have a winning coach, he's been a winning coach everywhere he's been at, whatever team you give he eventually starts to win," said McCoy on Speakeasy. "You get him a really, really good coordinator… you talk about an explosive offence, creative, we gave him that… The baggage last year was the offensive lineman was hurt, okay, now his offensive lineman is back, now they healthy.

"So all these things you got and we see worse results, so I got to talk about Herbert and I am a big fan of Herbert, but he has taken a step back. They gave you more things, more weapons, more linemen, a really good head coach, a really good offensive coordinator and you take a step back?"

Last season, with a depleted offensive line, Herbert threw for 3,727 yards and led the team to an 11-6 record. They made it only to the wildcard round but were eliminated, however, there was faith that with good players and a new offense, Herbert could help the Chargers, but that has not been the case so far.

The game against the Seahawks is going to be a tough one for the Chargers. For any chance of beating them, they will have to get Herbert back to his best. With all the criticism after the first three games, he will certainly be gunning for a big performance, and if that comes against the Seahawks, that could turn his and the team's fortunes around.

articles.title: New England Patriots sign OL Matt Pryor off Cardinals' practice squad
articles.summary: The Arizona Cardinals lost a veteran OL from their practice squad after he signs with another team's active roster.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals lost some veteran offensive line depth on Thursday. According to the NFL transaction report, the New England Patriots signed offensive lineman Matt Pryor to their active roster from Arizona's practice squad.

Pryor signed with the Cardinals in March and battled for a spot on the roster, but he was cut after the preseason and re-signed to the practice squad. He is an eight-year veteran who can play both guard and tackle.

He has 40 career starts, and he started 15 games in 2024 for the Chicago Bears at right guard.

Now the Cardinals have a vacancy on their 17-man practice squad. We will see if they make an addition on Friday or if they wait until next week to fill that spot.

articles.title: Tom Brady's obsession with longevity: The TB12 habits that kept him elite long after most quarterbacks were forced to retire
articles.summary: Tom Brady played 23 NFL seasons and won a Super Bowl at 43, an age when most quarterbacks are long gone from the league.
articles.body: Tom Brady played 23 NFL seasons and won a Super Bowl at 43, an age when most quarterbacks are long gone from the league. He retired for good in February 2023 at 45, after years of explaining the routine behind it all: the TB12 method, built with trainer Alex Guerrero. It centers on muscle pliability, a mostly plant-based diet, steady hydration and strict sleep. Some of it has drawn doubt from scientists. Still, the results are hard to ignore, so it is worth sorting out which habits likely mattered most and which ones did not.What TB12 habits kept Tom Brady elite long after most quarterbacks retire?The core idea behind the TB12 method is easy to explain. Brady wanted muscles that were long and soft, not just big and strong. He called it pliability. To get there, he leaned on foam rollers, resistance bands and a lot of hands-on body work. Heavy lifting was not the point. Moving well was.Food came next. Brady has said his plan leaned about 80 percent on vegetables, with little sugar, processed food or alcohol. He avoided nightshade vegetables like tomatoes and peppers, and he drank water all day. People laughed at the no-coffee rule and the avocado ice cream. Brady stuck with it anyway. He ate this way in season and out of it, for years.Sleep and recovery got the same respect. Brady has described going to bed early and treating rest as part of the job, not a reward for finishing it. That mindset matters. Plenty of athletes train hard and recover badly. He tried to do both well.Not every claim holds up. Scientists have questioned the nightshade rule, and pliability is more a brand term than a medical one. It also helps to remember that TB12 sells products and programs, so the claims come from people with something to sell. Treat those parts with caution. The basics, though, match what sports medicine teaches: sleep well, stay hydrated, eat real food and keep your joints moving.How much of Tom Brady's longevity came from habits and how much from his playing style?Habits explain only part of it. The way Brady played kept him safer than most. He read defenses before the snap, made decisions fast and got the ball out quickly. That meant fewer long holds in the pocket and fewer big hits. A quarterback who needs less time takes less punishment. It sounds obvious, but few players pull it off for two decades.The late numbers back this up. He won the MVP award in 2017 at age 40. He won Super Bowl LV with Tampa Bay at 43. In 2021, at 44, he led the NFL with 5,316 passing yards and 43 touchdown passes. Those were not farewell tours. They were simply very good seasons.What can a regular fan take from this? Probably not the private chef or the personal trainers. But sleep, water, mobility work and steady meals cost very little. The hard part is repetition, doing the dull things on the dull days.The next test is already on the field. Aaron Rodgers, now 42 and playing for the Steelers, is the league's most visible case of a quarterback trying to keep going deep into his forties. articles.title: Week 4 Waiver Wire Pickups and Available Sleepers in Most Yahoo and Sleeper Leagues
articles.summary: Week 4 got underway on Thursday night, and waiver wire claims have already been processed in most fantasy leagues. However, this doesn't mean that managers in need of help are completely out of luck.
articles.body:
Week 4 got underway on Thursday night, and waiver wire claims have already been processed in most fantasy leagues. However, this doesn't mean that managers in need of help are completely out of luck.

A few deep sleepers with Week 4 value are likely to remain available in most Yahoo and Sleeper leagues. A few more may be less attractive this week but are worth considering ahead of Week 5 byes.

Here, we'll examine the top remaining waiver-wire targets for point-per-reception (PPR) leagues.

Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones has had limited fantasy appeal to this point in 2026. His top receiver, Alec Pierce, is on injured reserve, and he hasn't carried as much value as a scrambler as he did in 2025.

Jones hasn't tallied more than 12.4 fantasy points in any of his first three outings this season. However, he projects as a strong streamer against the Washington Commanders this week.

Only the Detroit Lions have surrendered more fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks than Washington. San Darnold, in his first game back from injury, logged 29.7 against the Commanders last week.

Jones is rostered in 25 percent of fantasy leagues.

Mike Washington Jr., RB, Las Vegas Raiders

Even after recording 54 yards, one touchdown, and 11.4 fantasy points in Week 3, Mike Washington remains available in 60 percent of fantasy leagues. The Las Vegas Raiders running back is firmly behind starter Ashton Jeanty, which lowers his fantasy floor.

Washington yielded just 4.8 fantasy points over the first two weeks of the season combined.

However, Washington has a high ceiling as a change-of-pace back, one the Raiders should look to incorporate more often moving forward. Expect the Raiders to utilize both backs this week against the rival Kansas City Chiefs.

Kansas City has been middle-of-the-road against opposing RBs, allowing the 18th-most (tied) fantasy points to the position.

New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye has struggled with No. 1 receiver A.J. Brown out of the lineup, and his inability to find a new go-to target has been a big part of the problem. However, Maye found a bit of a rhythm with Mack Hollins in Week 3, though that wasn't nearly enough in New England's 35-6 loss.

Hollins caught six of nine targets for 87 yards against the Jacksonville Jaguars. He could have an even bigger outing against the Buffalo Bills this week.

The Patriots may need to throw early and often to keep pace with Josh Allen and the Bills. Hollins could also be extra motivated against his former team, one that has struggled against opposing receivers.

Buffalo has surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing WRs this season. Hollins is rostered in just six percent of fantasy leagues.

Tight end Darren Waller was a big part of the Carolina Panthers' game plan in Week 3 and should play a significant role again this week against the visiting Lions.

Against the Cleveland Browns, Waller caught five of eight targets for 51 yards. He should see a high volume of targets again this week, as receiver Jalen Coker continues to battle a quad injury.

Coker caught just two of four targets in Week 3 after catching eight of nine targets in each of the first two weeks.

Waller also has a terrific matchup this week, as no team has surrendered more fantasy points to TEs than Detroit. Waller is rostered in just 28 percent of fantasy leagues.

Bye weeks will enter the fantasy equation in Week 5. While the Panthers and Kansas City Chiefs are the only teams scheduled off, that means standouts like Bryce Young, Tetairoa McMillan Patrick Mahomes, Kenneth Walker III, and Travis Kelce wlll be unavailable. Planning ahead is far from the worst idea.

Here's a look at a few potential wire targets with reasonable or favorable Week 5 matchups:

Jameis Winston, QB, New York Giants (at WAS)

Jaylen Wright, RB, Miami Dolphins (vs. CIN)

Ollie Gordon II, RB, Miami Dolphins (vs. CIN)

Rashod Bateman, WR, Baltimore Ravens (at ATL)

Keenan Allen, WR, Indianapolis Colts (at PIT)

Terrance Ferguson, TE, Los Angeles Rams (vs. BUF)

articles.title: Jared Verse Calls Steelers 'Dirty' in Video, Reveals Trash Talk from Browns' Win in Rivalry Game
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns edge rusher Jared Verse is looking forward to a rematch against the Pittsburgh Steelers after what he described as "dirty" play during Thursday night's 27-24 win.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns edge rusher Jared Verse is looking forward to a rematch against the Pittsburgh Steelers after what he described as "dirty" play during Thursday night's 27-24 win.

"I'm like, 'Y'all double-teaming. Y'all sliding. Y'all garbage.' I was talking crazy to them," Verse told reporters Thursday night about the Steelers. "I don't got no respect for anybody that plays too dirty and that does too much extra s--t after the game, excuse my French.

"I can't wait to see them again. It's going to be a good time when I see them again."

Rodgers, McCarthy Explain Heated Exchange

Report Card Grades for the Browns' Big Win 📝

The Browns, who improved to 3-1 with the Week 4 victory, are set for a Week 8 rematch with the Steelers in Pittsburgh.

Verse said Thursday he felt the team he joined this June as part of the Myles Garrett trade wasn't "the old Browns."

"It's got new swag. We're a lot more aggressive. We're a lot more getting after it," Verse told reporters after the loss (h/t EWES' Camryn Justice ). "This is something different here."

Verse was already hyping up his team against the Steelers before Thursday's kickoff.

"I hate black and yellow, man. I hate it," Verse could be heard yelling to his defenders on the NFL on Prime broadcast.

Verse then clashed with Pittsburgh's offensive line at the end of the game in an altercation that involved him getting face-to-face with Mason McCormick before apparently taking a swing at the Steelers guard.

Steelers kicker Chris Boswell appeared upset when Verse wasn't called for a personal foul on the play.

Verse ultimately recorded two tackles, including one for loss. He finished the win with no pressures and no sacks while getting called for one unnecessary roughness penalty.

Verse will continue looking to record his first sack as a member of the Browns when Cleveland returns to action in Week 5 against the New York Jets.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels Out for Commanders vs. Colts, Latest Updates amid Elbow Injury Recovery
articles.summary: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels will miss Sunday's game in London against the Indianapolis Colts as he continues to recover from a dislocated elbow, head coach Dan Quinn announced Friday.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels will miss Sunday's game in London against the Indianapolis Colts as he continues to recover from a dislocated elbow, head coach Dan Quinn announced Friday.

After suffering a dislocated left elbow in a Week 2 loss against the Dallas Cowboys, Daniels didn't undergo surgery and wasn't placed on injured reserve. While he sat out Washington's Week 3 win over the Seattle Seahawks, Quinn announced that he would be able to travel and practice with the team ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts.

Top takeaways from Browns' win over Steelers

The injury marked Daniels' second dislocation in 10 months, as he injured the same elbow in a Week 9 loss to the Seahawks last November. Nicki Jhabvala of NFL.com noted that "exams of Daniels' elbow showed no fractures or any extensive damage to the surrounding ligaments, potentially allowing him to return more quickly instead of facing immediate surgery and a spot on injured reserve."

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that Daniels likely will need to undergo surgery after the 2026 season:

The Commanders would surely welcome Daniels back if he's ready to go, but veteran signal-caller Marcus Mariota proved that he can shoulder the load with a three-touchdown performance in the win over the Seahawks.

Daniels' next opportunity to line up under center will be in Week 5 against the New York Giants.

articles.title: From Andre the Giant to Tacko Fall: The case for using a 7-footer to block field goals
articles.summary: Decades ago, Washington floated the idea of bringing in Andre the Giant to block field goals. Now, the idea has been floated again, this time with 7-foot-7 T...
articles.body:
In spring of 1975, Washington coach George Allen hatched a plan to keep his NFL team in the headlines in the dead of the offseason.

Allen spread word that he was interested in signing professional wrestling behemoth Andre the Giant and developing him into a specialist at swatting field goals and extra points out of the air.

Washington quarterback Joe Theismann recalls being asked to pose for publicity photos beside Andre at a press luncheon organized by the team that July. The most famous photo features the 7-foot, more-than-400-pound wrestling icon effortlessly cradling Theisman like a toddler. Said Theismann with a laugh, "I've never been around another human being that large in my life."

The way Theismann remembers it, Allen's pursuit of Andre was more marketing ploy than serious courtship. There was never a tryout, Theismann said, nor a contract offer. Andre's drawing power barnstorming the country as professional wrestling's ultimate attraction brought him far more money than he ever could have earned in those days from playing NFL football.

"George Allen was the ultimate promoter," Theismann told Yahoo Sports. "Back in the 1970s, you didn't have football 24-7-365 like you do now. When the season ended, there was a time when there was a lull, but George always wanted to find creative ways to keep the Washington Redskins' name front of mind."

An idea that started as a harebrained publicity stunt half a century ago has since resurfaced as a radically unconventional strategic proposal. A former NFL assistant coach and director of football analytics posted to social media earlier this week encouraging teams to give 7-foot-7 former NBA center Tacko Fall a tryout as a field goal block specialist.

The notion of deploying someone like Fall in this role first struck Ryan Paganetti nine years ago when he was part of Doug Pederson's Philadelphia Eagles coaching staff. A fellow coach in a special teams meeting emphasized the potential for interior rushers to block a field goal if they're able to generate two yards of push and get their hands up. That made Paganetti wonder how much more disruptive that interior rush could be if it cleared space for a long-armed, bouncy-legged 7-footer with a basketball background.

Since NFL rules prohibit defenders from lining up directly over the long snapper on field-goal or extra-point attempts, Paganetti proposes putting two interior defensive linemen on one guard and tasking them with driving him backward as far as possible. Then Fall or another similarly gigantic human would rush into the lane they've created, extend his arms and attempt to time his jump to meet the kick.

The concept was zany enough that Paganetti didn't dare mention it as a 27-year-old Eagles assistant linebackers coach just a few years out of Dartmouth. As the economics major-turned-football analytics savant says now, "You can't walk into the head coach's or GM's office and suggest something that would sound bats**** crazy. Then they just laugh at you and you have no credibility for the rest of your career."

What Paganetti wisely did instead was bide his time while waiting for technology to come along that enabled him to quantify his idea. Gradually, he became more comfortable pitching colleagues on the notion of 7-footers as special teams weapons.

Trusted friends across the industry were receptive. One special teams coordinator who worked with Paganetti was not.

"I will literally freak the f— out if you bring that up to [the head coach or general manager]," Paganetti recalls the special teams coordinator telling him. "I don't want to have to worry about coaching that s***."

Now in his first year working as an independent football analytics and strategy consultant after previous stints with the Eagles, Jaguars and Raiders, Paganetti decided the timing was right to go public with his idea.

"Could the tallest player in NBA Combine history change the outcome of a Super Bowl?" Paganetti wrote to begin a 593-word X post on Tuesday evening.

That post now has more than one million views.

"If you want to be innovative, you have to be willing to think outside the box," Paganetti said, "and you have to be willing to be laughed at."

1 in 4 games decided by a field goal or less

The tallest NFL player ever deployed as a field-goal block weapon seldom rushed the kicker from the line of scrimmage.

In 1969, Kansas City Chiefs coach Hank Stram would position 6-foot-10 rookie tight end Morris Stroud under the goal posts and have him try to time his leap to deflect the ball as it approached the crossbar.

The NFL quickly intervened and banned Stroud's goaltending tactic before the former Clark Atlanta University basketball player blocked a single NFL kick. The rulebook now bans players from leaping up to bat away a kick as it passes over the crossbar and grants permission to the referee to award three points for that "palpably unfair act."

The best current demonstration that height can be an advantage when blocking field goals in the NFL is Calais Campbell, the long, nimble 6-foot-8, 307-pound defensive end who has swatted 10 kicks out of the air since 2009. Campbell has earned the freedom from special teams coordinators to dictate where he lines up on any field-goal block try because of his unique blend of reach, strength and innate sense for where the path of the ball might be.

Campbell's height is an outlier among pass-rush specialists because of his unique ability to maximize the advantages of his extraordinary length while still moving explosively and getting low enough not to sacrifice leverage. Most athletes 6-8 or taller would be fighting against physics because their center of gravity is so much higher than the average 6-4, 310-pound offensive lineman.

Those issues help explain why no NFL team has experimented with a 7-footer as a field goal blocker before. That player would almost certainly have to be a specialist who could not be counted on to contribute in other ways.

It's Paganetti's contention that a 7-foot-7 giant like Fall would be worth rostering if he could be developed into a special teams weapon. Roughly one-in-four NFL games are decided by three points or fewer. A team significantly increasing its field-goal block rate from the standard 1.9% could be worth an extra victory or two. Then there's the potential intimidation factor, which could also reduce accuracy and prove meaningful.

"It's definitely worth the last spot on a 53-man roster if a guy can do this at a high rate," Paganetti said. "Honestly, it's probably worth like the 30th roster spot."

What combination of height, reach and vertical jump would a 7-footer need to strike fear into NFL kickers? The best way to quantify that comes from a sports technology company founded in Denmark by golf-enthusiast brothers Klaus Eldrup-Jørgensen and Morten Eldrup-Jørgensen, along with radar engineer Fredrik Tuxen.

Harnessing Tuxen's expertise in using Doppler radar to track bullets and missiles, the founders of TrackMan created a reliable way to reconstruct the trajectory, velocity and movement of a golf ball. Then TrackMan began applying its precision tracking system to other sports. The Chicago Bears became the first NFL team to use TrackMan in 2019 when evaluating kickers to replace Cody Parkey. Now, special teams coaches from all 32 NFL teams receive TrackMan data reports on kickers and punters at events like the NFL Scouting Combine.

The average ball height on NFL field-goal attempts after seven yards is just shy of 12 feet, according to Simon Mathiesen, head of TrackMan's football operations. About 80% of NFL field-goal attempts are 11-13 feet off the ground after seven yards, Mathiesen said. Seven yards is the relevant data point in Mathiesen's eyes because NFL kickers tend to kick from eight yards behind the line of scrimmage and field-goal defenses typically generate one yard of push.

At the 2019 NBA Draft combine, Fall stood 7-7 in shoes with a standing reach of 10 feet, 2½ inches. Throw in a reported 26.5-inch vertical leap, admittedly without a helmet and football gear to weigh him down, and Fall would clear the 12-foot mark with ease.

"Theoretically, I think it's worth exploring," said Mathiesen, a former All-American kicker at Division II Northwest Missouri State. "If I were a GM, I think I'd look for the most athletic 7-footer I can find and test him out in the preseason. Is that more valuable in a preseason game than a sixth-string receiver? I certainly think so."

Paganetti gently pushes back against the TrackMan estimate that the field-goal block unit typically generates only one yard of push. He argues that the interior rush often pushes the offensive line back two yards — and that such a push should happen more often if the defenders driving the guard backward don't have to worry about jumping or getting their hands up.

NFL player tracking data has the ability to measure how far backward a guard is typically driven on a double-team rush, but Paganetti has not found time to study that yet. If he's right that the push is often two yards instead of just one, that would mean that the ball is crossing that spot about 10 feet off the ground instead of nearly 12.

"I feel very good saying that 12 feet is way too high," Paganetti said. "I don't think there's actually been a single block where any player was 12 feet high. I'm not even sure there's been a single block where any player was 11 feet high. The rush is getting more movement than that."

In July 2025, someone actually dabbled with Paganetti's concept before he had the chance.

University of Florida special teams coach Joe Houston received permission to have 7-9 men's basketball walk-on Olivier Rioux participate in practice and attempt to block some kicks from Gators kicker Hunter Smith.

The experiment didn't last long. Houston eventually scrapped it, reportedly because Rioux's vertical was just 11 inches and even with his extra-long reach, the former world's tallest teenager was unable to block any kicks.

"They were a little disappointed," Florida men's basketball coach Todd Golden told the Associated Press.

By then, so many of Paganetti's friends knew about his obsession with this idea that he received a half-dozen texts containing links to articles about this experiment. Paganetti loved to see Florida giving the concept a try, but he said he wishes he could talk to Houston or former Florida head coach Billy Napier about some of the nuances that went unreported.

"It's unclear if they basically just messed around with him standing at the line of scrimmage, or if they actually had more of a plan," Paganetti said.

Yahoo Sports also sought further clarity from Napier and Houston, both of whom have since left Florida and moved on to other jobs. Houston is the best person to speak with, Napier said via a James Madison football spokesperson. An LSU football spokesperson did not return multiple messages seeking comment from Houston.

To Paganetti, finding the right 7-footer is as important as having a savvy scheme. He argues NFL teams would need to target someone with the ball skills and coordination to be able to time their jump and the girth and toughness to be able to withstand a hit. The 7-footer can't be so athletic that he's NBA-caliber, yet also can't be such a plodding stiff that he can't make explosive movements.

In other words, Tacko Fall. The 7-foot-7 center last appeared in an NBA regular-season game as a member of the Cleveland Cavaliers on December 30, 2021. He has since played professional basketball in China, where he has twice led the league in blocked shots. Fall received an invitation to training camp with the Philadelphia 76ers but is a long shot to make the roster.

It's unclear if Fall would have any interest in donning a football helmet and shoulder pads. Even if he did, some in football circles are unconvinced that his presence would prove disruptive for field-goal kicking operations.

"If NFL teams decided to start signing former 7-foot-plus basketball players specially to block field goals, I don't believe it would significantly change the percentage of blocked kicks," said retired former NFL kicker Nick Novak, now a private kicking coach and showcase host in the San Diego area.

Height over the line of scrimmage was always a major point of emphasis for Novak during his playing days when preparing for teams with proven field-goal block specialists. Special teams coaches would position him as close as five yards from the crossbar, forcing him to either clear it or risk the ball ricocheting back at him. Nowadays, Novak's pupils use TrackMan to measure the trajectory of their kicks.

"A great operation combined with great blocking from the field-goal protection team prevents penetration up the middle and pressure off the edge," Novak said. "You don't want a kicker changing his normal ball or trajectory because there happens to be a 7-footer on the other side."

Count former NFL special teams coach Gary Zauner among those who are skeptical that any team will ever roster a 7-footer as a field-goal block specialist. Zauner questioned if such a player would get a hand on enough kicks to prove worthy of taking up a roster spot. The former Vikings, Ravens and Cardinals special teams coach also pointed out that an astute team could kick from nine yards behind the line of scrimmage instead of eight if it sought to lessen the threat of an on-rushing 7-footer.

"Devin Hester caused me to lose sleep," Zauner said. "I don't think this would cause me to lose any sleep."

Theismann isn't as quick to dismiss Paganetti's idea as Zauner is. For decades, the former Washington quarterback has wondered what sort of impact Andre the Giant might have made if Allen were serious about pursuing him, if it wasn't just a publicity stunt. Now, Theismann wonders if Victor Wembanyama's presence on a field-goal block unit would be as terrifying for kickers as him lurking near the rim is for opposing guards attacking off the dribble.

"I would love to see it happen just because of my curiosity," Theismann said. "Certainly people would be talking about it."

articles.title: Week 4 NFL betting, odds: Picks against the spread, winners for every game from a blended AI model
articles.summary: We asked an AI model with four sets of NFL power ratings blended together to pick the against-the-spread winner of every Week 4 NFL game. Here are the result...
articles.body:
Week 4 of the NFL season kicked off on Thursday night, as Deshaun Watson and the Cleveland Browns improved to 3-1 on the season with an impressive 27-24 win against Aaron Rodgers' Pittsburgh Steelers as a three-point home underdog.

How will the rest of the weekend's games play out?

We used a blended model with four NFL power ratings, including ESPN's FPI and FTN Fantasy's DVOA rankings , and asked Claude to simulate the final score of every Week 4 game and give a brief write-up of why the game would play out that way. We also asked it to list the against-the-spread winner and if the game went over or under the total.

Here are the results for every Week 4 game:

Indianapolis Colts (-4, 48.5) vs. Washington Commanders ( in London )

The market has Indianapolis by four, but my ratings have it closer to a pick'em. Both defenses are bad: Indianapolis allows +19.2% DVOA and Washington +8.3%. Both teams give up about 30 points per game, so this should be high-scoring. The Colts' special teams (+9.4%) give them a slight edge on a neutral field, but Washington getting four points is the better value.

Projected score: Colts 26, Commanders 25

Tennessee Titans at Baltimore Ravens (-12, 42.5)

Baltimore's offense is third in DVOA (+28.1%) and scores 30.7 points per game. Tennessee is 0-3, scores 12.3 PPG and has one of the league's worst special teams units (-11.0%). The Ravens win comfortably, but the model's 11-point margin is half a point short of the spread, so the Titans cover only barely. The over is steadier: Baltimore's defense is only average, so Tennessee should reach 17 points.

New England Patriots at Buffalo Bills (-6.5, 48.5)

Buffalo's offense (+37.5% DVOA) should dominate a Patriots offense that ranks last (-29.9%) after a 35-6 loss at Jacksonville. New England's defense is good (eighth), and Buffalo's (22nd) just survived a minus-four turnover game, which keeps this from being a blowout. The model's 6.6-point margin lands just past the new number, so the Bills cover by a hair. Treat it as a lean, not a pick. New England scores only 12 per game, which keeps the total near 45, under 48.5.

Jacksonville Jaguars at Cincinnati Bengals (-2.5, 51.5)

This is a coin flip, and Jacksonville's defense tips it. The Jaguars rank second in DVOA (+43.1%) and allow just 12 points per game. Cincinnati is good (+18.8%, seventh) but allows 21 per game and is only favored on home field. Jacksonville plus 2.5 is solid value. The total of 51 is the highest on the slate, but one elite defense points to about 47.

Arizona Cardinals (-2.5, 44) at New York Giants

The market has Arizona favored, but its defense is 31st in DVOA (+21.9%) and allows 27 points per game. The Giants' offense is poor (-16.0%), but their special teams (+9.4%, second) can swing a close game. My composite ratings have New York slightly ahead. Both offenses are limited, so the model projects under 44.

Projected score: Giants 22, Cardinals 20

New York Jets at Chicago Bears (-3.5, 43)

Chicago scores 29.7 per game and allows 17.7, and its offense is eighth in DVOA. The Bears beat Philadelphia 27-7 last week with Case Keenum at quarterback. The Jets just lost to Detroit and have poor special teams (-7.4%, 28th). The model projects a five-point Chicago win, covering -3.5. The Bears alone should score about 25, and the Jets get to 20, which clears 43.

Dallas Cowboys at Houston Texans (-3, 48)

Dallas has a top-five offense (+22.6% DVOA, 29.3 points per game) but a bad defense (27th). Houston is 0-3, though DVOA still ranks it 17th. My composite ratings give Dallas a slight edge, so the Cowboys' +3 is the value side. The model projects 49 total points, just over 48, which makes the over the thinnest lean on the board.

Los Angeles Rams (-3.5, 43) at Philadelphia Eagles

The Rams' DVOA (+13.9%, 10th) is better than their 1-2 record, with a top-five defense. But their special teams are last in the league (-13.0%), and they blew a 16-0 lead to Denver. Philadelphia scores 18.3 per game after a 27-7 loss to Chicago, but it's home. With the total at 43, one extra score or a special-teams play tips this to the over, but treat it as a very thin lean.

Green Bay Packers (-3.5, 39) at Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Green Bay is the clear pick with Baker Mayfield out. The Packers' defense is the main reason, even though their DVOA is a modest +12.8%. Tampa Bay's 20.7 points per game came with Mayfield, and a rookie making his first start should score less. Jalon Daniels' rushing ability and a simplified game plan around Emeka Egbuka and Bucky Irving help a little. The model's 4.4-point margin clears 3.5, but only by about a point, so it's a lean. Both offenses are mediocre, but the model projects about 41, a couple of points over 39.

Projected score: Packers 23, Buccaneers 18

Miami Dolphins at Minnesota Vikings (-10.5, 39)

Miami is last in every rating I used and scores just 12 PPG. Minnesota is 3-0, has the league's best defense (-30.3% DVOA) and best special teams (+12.8%), and its blitz-heavy scheme under Brian Flores is creating short fields. The model projects a 12-point win, narrowly covering 11. The Vikings' offense is weak (-25.8%), which limits the margin. Defensive or return scores push the total past 39.

Projected score: Vikings 26, Dolphins 14

Kansas City Chiefs (-4.5, 47.5) at Las Vegas Raiders

Kansas City is 3-0, fourth in DVOA and allows 16.7 points per game. Las Vegas has a good defense (-10.3%) and special teams (+5.6%), but an average offense. The model has the Chiefs winning by four, half a point short of the number, so the Raiders cover. Two solid defenses project about 46 points, under 47.5.

Los Angeles Chargers at Seattle Seahawks (-7, 42.5)

The Chargers are 0-3, have scored fewer than 20 points in six straight games and rank 31st in DVOA. Seattle has the third-best defense (-20.9%), allows 16.7 per game and is coming off its first loss in 13 games. The model projects an 8-point win, covering 7 narrowly. Seattle's offense (25 per game) should reach the mid-20s, and Los Angeles needs only about 17 to push the total over 42.5.

Projected score: Seahawks 26, Chargers 18

Denver Broncos at San Francisco 49ers (-2.5, 48)

San Francisco leads DVOA at +68.7%, with a historically good passing offense. ESPN's FPI makes the 49ers a 7.9-point favorite, so 2.5 looks short. Denver has a below-average offense (-6.8%) and averages 20 points per game, despite its comeback against the Rams. The model has San Francisco winning by about 6.5. Both defenses are solid, so the total lands near 47, a slight lean under 48.

Two good offenses meet two bad defenses. Detroit scores 31 per game but allows 31.7 (28th in DVOA). Carolina scores 29.7 per game, and Bryce Young leads the league in passing yards. The model gives Detroit just a one-point edge, so Carolina covers at home. With both defenses leaking points, the model's 53 total points beats the posted 51.

Both teams are in the bottom third of the league. Atlanta jumped to 23rd in DVOA after beating Green Bay, but scores only 17 per game. The Saints rate slightly higher on FPI, nfelo and DVOA, so they win, but a two-point margin doesn't cover 2.5. Atlanta's weak offense keeps the total near 46, under 47.5.

articles.title: New Marvin Harrison Jr. Trade Rumors on Cardinals WR's Future Ahead of 2026 NFL Deadline
articles.summary: Rival teams continue to wonder about the availability of Marvin Harrison Jr. despite the Arizona Cardinals not yet placing the third-year wide receiver on the trade block, ESPN's Dan Graziano reported Friday.
articles.body:
Rival teams continue to wonder about the availability of Marvin Harrison Jr. despite the Arizona Cardinals not yet placing the third-year wide receiver on the trade block, ESPN's Dan Graziano reported Friday.

Harrison has received just nine targets through a three-game stretch during which Jacoby Brissett has seemingly favored tight end Trey McBride and wideouts Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne.

According to Graziano, "the perception of Harrison from people around the league is that he isn't a fit in an Arizona offense that prioritizes McBride as its top target, and that has led some teams to think he might be available."

Players Who Could Use a Change of Scenery 🏈

Graziano noted the Cardinals themselves "have given no indication that they are eager or even interested in trading Harrison."

Should the Cardinals eventually decide to shop Harrison, there would be "plenty" of interested teams, Graziano reported.

Graziano's report follows the Cardinals' Week 3 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, during which Harrison recorded season highs in both targets (five) and receptions (three) while recording 40 receiving yards.

He was flagged for offensive pass interference early in the game, but later caught a 19-yard pass from Brissett on a fourth-quarter touchdown drive.

"Trying to find more ways to get him the ball. I thought he played pretty well last game. Every time his number was called, he made the play," Brissett said about Harrison ahead of Week 4. "That was a big third down for us, and threw it with the utmost confidence."

When asked if he ever talked with Brissett during a game about being open on plays when he wasn't targeted, Harrison said , "Maybe during the week... but definitely not on a Sunday or gametime. You let them do their process, go through their progression, their reads... to tell someone, 'Hey, just look at me,' that's not winning football."

Harrison, selected by the Cardinals with the No. 4 pick in the 2024 draft, is playing on a rookie contract that remains under team control through the 2028 season. The Cardinals have both McBride and Wilson under contract through 2029.

Whether the Cardinals ultimately decide to move Harrison to a team willing to bet he can develop into a WR1 with a change of scenery could depend both on his usage down the stretch and whether Arizona (1-2) is within postseason contention by the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

articles.title: Cowboys' Jerry Jones Explains Decision to Trade for Joey Porter Jr., Give up 2nd-Round Draft Pick
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones says he is hoping his latest trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers will have similar results to his 2025 deal for wide receiver George Pickens.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones says he is hoping his latest trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers will have similar results to his 2025 deal for wide receiver George Pickens.

Jones discussed his decision to trade a 2027 sixth-rounder and 2028 second-rounder to the Steelers in exchange for cornerback Joey Porter Jr. during his Friday appearance on 105.3 The Fan .

"We hope that this is not only an improvement in, just generally, our personnel, but we hope it really can be one that he really finds his level," Jones said.

Rodgers, McCarthy Explain Heated Exchange

Players Who Could Use a Change of Scenery 🏈

Jones continued, "I would hope it would mirror maybe the George Pickens move that brought him in. I know that's a pretty high bar, that's pretty high expectations, but you have to have 'em to make a trade like this."

There was a reported split between Pickens and Steelers leadership before he was traded to Dallas, where he recorded the best season of his career in 2025.

The Cowboys will now hope to see a similar resurgence from another disgruntled former Steelers player in Porter, who said he felt disrespected by failed extension talks with the franchise prior to his own trade.

After the trade, the Cowboys are set to select just four times in the 2027 draft. The Steelers are set to make nine picks, including three initially belonging to the Cowboys, per Tankathon .

Quarterback Dak Prescott said after the deal that "to make a win-now trade, it means a lot" to the Cowboys after a 1-2 start to the season (h/t The Athletic's Jon Machota ).

"It just shows you that this whole organization is on the same page. You're thankful when you got guys at the top, the owners, making those decisions and not waiting," Prescott said Thursday, per Machota.

Jones agreed with Prescott in his Friday radio appearance.

"He's accurately got it pegged. It is a belief in where we are and what we can do right now," Jones said.

The Cowboys are dealing with an injury-thinned secondary in which cornerbacks Cobie Durant and Shavon Revel Jr. have yet to practice this week due to injury.

Porter is still looking to make his season debut after sitting out the Steelers' first three games with what the team reported was a back injury.

Coach Brian Schottenheimer said in his own radio appearance the Cowboys are "hoping" Porter can play Sunday but will wait to see how he feels after Friday's practice.

The Cowboys are preparing for a Sunday afternoon road game against the winless Houston Texans. Kickoff is slated for 1 p.m. ET in Houston.

articles.title: CBS and Tony Romo mutually part ways more than two months after Romo's OWI arrest
articles.summary: Romo was pulled over and charged with OWI on July 23.
articles.body:
The awkward holding pattern between CBS and Tony Romo is over.

CBS announced that it is parting ways with Romo, who had been its No. 1 NFL color commentator with play-by-play announcer Jim Nantz. Romo was arrested on suspicion of operating while intoxicated on July 23 after a golf event in Wisconsin and had been on leave from the network. J.J. Watt took over No. 1 color duties on CBS' top NFL broadcasts through the first three weeks of the regular season. Romo pleaded no contest to OWI charges on Sept. 1.

"CBS Sports and Tony Romo have mutually agreed to part ways," CBS' statement said. "We thank Tony for his contributions over the past nine years and wish him the best moving forward.

"JJ Watt will continue to partner with Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson on our lead NFL announce team for the rest of the season. All other teams remain the same, including Ian Eagle, Ross Tucker and Evan Washburn."

Romo added a statement to Front Office Sports, saying he was going to take a break and focus on his health and family before pursuing another opportunity.

In a statement on the same day as he pleaded no contest to the charges, Romo said he had developed a reliance on pain medication after multiple back surgeries stemming from injuries sustained during his playing career as quarterback of the Dallas Cowboys. He said efforts to get off those medications led to an "over-reliance" on alcohol.

"None of this is an excuse," Romo said in the statement. "These are my failures, and I take responsibility for them."

Romo joined CBS in 2017, shortly after his 13-year career with the Cowboys ended. He was immediately placed on the No. 1 NFL broadcasting team and his enthusiasm and ability to call out plays before they happened made him an instant star in broadcasting. In 2020, CBS and Romo agreed to a 10-year contract for $180 million.

Reviews on Romo's performance in the booth had waned in recent seasons, which might have led CBS to look for a way out of Romo's large contract with four years left on it.

articles.title: Tony Romo out at CBS Sports after nine years following drunk driving arrest
articles.summary: Former NFL star Tony Romo will not be returning to CBS Sports after his arrest for drunk driving earlier this summer, the network said in a statement.
articles.body: Former NFL star Tony Romo will not be returning to CBS Sports after his arrest for drunk driving earlier this summer, the network said in a statement. CBS Sports and Romo “mutually agreed to part ways,” according to the statement, after nine years of the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback featuring as one of CBS’ top voices during NFL games. “We thank Tony for his contributions over the past nine years and wish him the best moving forward,” the statement read. Romo was arrested in July on suspicion of operating a vehicle while intoxicated in Wisconsin, a moment that stained his image as the aw-shucks, clean-cut football star who has become one of the best on-air personalities in the game. He pleaded no contest last month to a civil offense for operating while intoxicated. In his own statement, Romo said he was proud of his time at CBS Sports but needed time to get himself right after the brush with the law. “I approached my role as a game analyst the way I’ve approached everything in my life–with a desire to win and be the best that I can be,” Romo said in the statement. “I’m going to use this time to take a break, something I’ve never done before, and focus on my health and my family before moving on to my next opportunity. I am grateful for my time with CBS Sports and for the continued support of my family and friends, as well as the NFL community and fans.” After his plea of no contest, Romo said he had begun relying on alcohol to help deal with the constant pain left over from his playing career. He said at the time that he planned to use the lessons from football to help move on from the arrest and figure out the next steps in his life. “The past month has been difficult, but it has also been personally significant. It has required me to confront and own my mistakes fully—to the Lord, to myself, to my family, and now to the public,” he wrote. “I am working closely with a team of doctors to address my health and make the necessary changes. I am deeply grateful for the support of my family, my friends, and the NFL community, including players, coaches, and owners. Your encouragement has meant more to me than you know.”
