articles.title: NFL London Games 2026: Marcus Mariota to start for Washington Commanders vs Indianapolis Colts as Jayden Daniels ruled out
articles.summary: Marcus Mariota will make his second start of the NFL season in London as he steps in for injured quarterback Jayden Daniels for Washington Commanders' clash against Indianapolis Colts at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Sunday; watch live at 2pm on Sky Sports NFL
articles.body:
Head coach Dan Quinn announced the decision on Friday after practice at the team's hotel accommodations outside London.

Daniels returned to practice this week after dislocating his elbow in Week Two against the Dallas Cowboys. He's been wearing a protective brace and had expressed no concerns about further damage, but the Commanders will hold him out for at least one more game.

"[Daniels] had a great week. It was awesome to have him back on the field in a limited fashion," Quinn said. "He'll be out. Marcus will start."

Quinn called Daniels' return to practice "a huge positive step for him and for us."

"We'll assess where we are next week when we get to a full week of practice all the way through," the coach said.

Last week, Mariota threw three touchdown passes in the 33-31 win over the reigning champion Seattle Seahawks.

Daniels' elbow dislocation was the second in as many seasons for Daniels, who missed most of the second half of last season with the same injury.

The third-year quarterback, who led the Commanders to the NFC Championship Game in his rookie season, had said on Thursday he was preparing mentally to start against the Colts and wasn't worried about re-injuring the elbow.

"That's what the brace is for," Daniels said.

The Commanders host the New York Giants on Sunday, October 11. The team has a bye in Week Seven.

"Certainly, anytime you can practice, that's a big deal," Quinn said. "So for him to get back, that was a big step for us. Typical for him, he's more ready than you'd expect. That's just kind of how he is."

Quinn was asked what he needs to see to put Daniels back on the field, and said: "It's really just like an entire group medical performance.

"Where he's at, the practice part was a big piece of that today. But next week we're planning for him to get a full week of practice. That would be a big deal for us."

Speaking on this week's edition of Inside The Huddle , Neil Reynolds and Phoebe Schecter looked ahead to the game with both teams coming off wins in Week Three.

"When you come off a win you get a little bit of a different schedule, but you have hope and they both really needed these wins, especially the Commanders. The confidence that should give them, especially having Mariota at quarterback. That is exactly what we need going into these International games," said Schecter.

The Colts have an offence still without wide receiver Alec Pierce and are waiting for quarterback Daniel Jones to get up to the speed of last year.

"They're not the same without an explosive running game," explained Schecter. "So much of that team is run through Jonathan Taylor and they're struggling to get the ball going consistently. He has his sparks but there's nothing that's consistent. That's forcing Daniel Jones into this uncomfortable position because right now your top players are Josh Downs and tight end Tyler Warren. That also limits where you're able to throw it on the field.

"Other than that you got [Laquon] Treadwell, Keenan Allen. I mean if you're this Commanders defence, you're coming into it saying: 'We're going to take away everything inside and we're going to force you to throw it outside to your lesser receiver and out you under pressure.'

"We've read that book before and saw it a couple of times last year when people felt they had Daniel Jones' number.

"It should be a high-scoring game but I'm going to go with the Commanders."

Reynolds said: "This is a game that Jonathan Taylor takes over. They don't attack Washington through the air because they don't have the weapons so this is a big Jonathan Taylor game. He's going to touch the ball at least 30 times, so give me the Indianapolis Colts."

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy Reacts to 'Shock' of Giants Trade in 1st Comments Since Leaving Vikings
articles.summary: New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy was caught off guard by Monday's trade from the Minnesota Vikings.
articles.body:
New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy was caught off guard by Monday's trade from the Minnesota Vikings.

McCarthy said the trade was a "shock" but that he sees his arrival with the Giants as an "opportunity," per ESPN's Jordan Raanan.

"I didn't anticipate it. But at the end of the day, it's an opportunity. It's an opportunity to take advantage of," McCarthy said, per The Athletic's Charlotte Carroll .

McCarthy continued, per Carroll : "I'm extremely blessed. You know, I'm extremely grateful for all the time in Minnesota. You know, so many great relationships, so many learning lessons and growth. I'm just so fired up to be a New York football Giant."

The Giants traded a fifth-round to the Vikings in order to acquire McCarthy after losing Jaxson Dart to a season-ending knee injury.

McCarthy, who started 10 games for the Vikings last season, had been relegated to a third-string option behind Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz in Minnesota.

Coach John Harbaugh said last weekend Jameis Winston, who has led the Giants to a 2-1 start to the season, would remain starter for the immediate future.

Harbaugh said Friday the Giants are still working on determining whether McCarthy will serve as a second- or third-string quarterback, per Raanan .

McCarthy joined the Giants for a practice open to media for this first time this Wednesday. He was third in quarterback drills behind Winston and Jake Haener, per Greg Johnson of the Trentonian .

Giants offensive coordinator Matt Nagy said Thursday he was impressed with McCarthy's ability to quickly adjust to a new offense.

"You're basically taking all of OTAs just trying to learn the foundation, which guys have done in five or six months, and now taking that into two days," Nagy said. "He's done a great job with it. We're impressed."

As McCarthy continues adjusting to his new team, Winston will remain under center for the Giants when the team kicks off a Week 4 matchup against the visiting Arizona Cardinals this Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Tony Romo and CBS part ways but history suggests former NFL QB will add to his career comeback mark
articles.summary: Tony Romo's CBS Sports exit after his OWI arrest and plea deal may cost him tens of millions, but history suggests a broadcast booth comeback.
articles.body: Tony Romo and CBS Sports have mutually agreed to part ways, which was expected following the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback's OWI arrest and plea deal in July and September. But history suggests Romo will eventually be able to do in the broadcast booth what he did 25 times with the Cowboys: author a comeback. That assumes he wants to do that, which seems likely. JIM NANTZ SPEAKS OUT ON 'GREAT FRIEND' TONY ROMO'S OWI ARREST, SAYS HE WILL 'ALWAYS' BE THERE FOR HIM First the news announced by both CBS Sports and Romo in separate statements: "CBS Sports and Tony Romo have mutually agreed to part ways," CBS said in a statement on Friday. "We thank Tony for his contributions over the past nine years and wish him the best moving forward. "J.J. Watt will continue to partner with Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson on our lead NFL announce team for the rest of the season." Said Romo in his own statement: "I’m proud of what I accomplished at CBS Sports over the last nine years. I approached my role as a game analyst the way I’ve approached everything in my life – with a desire to win and be the best that I can be. "I’m going to use this time to take a break, something I’ve never done before, and focus on my health and my family before moving on to my next opportunity. I am grateful for my time with CBS Sports and for the continued support of my family and friends, as well as the NFL community and fans." This needs some context. The remaining portion of that was worth approximately $70-$75 million. So Romo's Wisconsin intoxication folly almost definitely cost him a lot of money. But the obvious misstep doesn't need to be thought of as a permanent misstep, if Romo indeed gets himself sorted and wants to return to an NFL analyst chair. He's also a bigger name who, oddly, gains more attention because of his arrest. So, it is quite possible that after some time away, Romo will be able to return in one of those roles. The point is sports television is generally forgiving because the audience is likewise forgiving. Romo, 46, is currently without driving privileges, which were revoked for six months, he must complete an alcohol-assessment program, install an ignition-interlock device, and he's already paid court costs and fees. articles.title: 49ers Owner Jed York Suspended for 6 Games After His Arrest in Prostitution Sting
articles.summary: SANTA CLARA, Calif. (AP) — The NFL suspended San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York for six games Friday following his arrest earlier this year in a prostitution sting in Ohio.
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. (AP) — The NFL suspended San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York for six games Friday following his arrest earlier this year in a prostitution sting in Ohio.

The league announced that York also was fined $500,000 for violating the league's personal conduct policy. York has not attended any games or league meetings so far this season and was credited with three games served. He is eligible to return on Oct. 20, following the team's game the previous night against Washington. The NFL's fall league meetings begin that day in New York.

York said in a statement released by the team that he accepts the punishment given by the league and apologized for his actions.

"To my family, to the players, coaches, and employees of the San Francisco 49ers, to our fans and partners, I am deeply sorry," he said. "This was an inexcusable mistake and I take full responsibility. What I did does not reflect my values or the man I strive to be for my family. While I fell short of the model I want to set for my sons, I now hope to show them the importance of owning up to one's failures, and that even our worst moments teach us to be better. Leading the 49ers is a privilege, and one I don't take lightly. Your trust will have to be earned back over time, and I look forward to that work ahead."

York was arrested in a mobile home park by the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force after police said he was attempting to pay $160 for sex with a woman he believed to be a prostitute.

York was booked into jail and was released after posting a $5,000 bond. York was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct. He pleaded no contest to that charge and to possessing criminal tools for using his phone to respond to an undercover online prostitution advertisement.

He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offenses to be served concurrently and was credited with one day served when he pleaded no contest. He also was fined $1,150. Police seized the $160 from York and that was later given to the human trafficking task force as part of the plea. York also completed an online course.

Owners have been previously punished for violating the personal conduct policy. The late Indianapolis Colts owner Jim Irsay was suspended for six games and fined $500,000 following a guilty plea to driving while impaired in 2014.

New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft was investigated but not punished by the league after he was arrested in Florida in 2019 for allegedly paying for sex with a woman at a massage parlor. The charge was later dropped after a court ruled that police violated the rights of Kraft and the other customers when they secretly installed video cameras inside massage rooms at the spa.

York spent most of the summer in Ohio, where he grew up near Youngstown and had been away from the team even before his arrest. He had filed for divorce from his wife, Danielle, in May, according to court records.

York took over day-to-day control of the 49ers from his parents in 2008. He became the team's principal owner in 2024. After some initial struggles under York's leadership, the team has been a consistent contender since hiring coach Kyle Shanahan and general manager John Lynch in 2017.

The Niners have made the Super Bowl three times under York's leadership, losing in the 2012 season under coach Jim Harbaugh and the 2019 and '23 seasons under Shanahan and Lynch.

York also oversaw the building of Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara. The team moved from San Francisco to the new stadium in 2014. The stadium has hosted two Super Bowls, a World Cup and a College Football Playoff title game.

articles.title: Aaron Donald Injured, Latest Update on Rams Star's Back, Status vs. Eagles
articles.summary: Sunday's marquee matchup between the Los Angeles Rams and Philadelphia Eagles is losing a lot of star power due to injuries, with Aaron Donald joining the group of players not playing.
articles.body:
Sunday's marquee matchup between the Los Angeles Rams and Philadelphia Eagles is losing a lot of star power due to injuries, with Aaron Donald joining the group of players not playing.

Rams head coach Sean McVay announced on Friday that a back injury will keep Donald out against the Eagles.

Donald was listed as a DNP on the Rams' official practice report for Wednesday and Thursday.

McVay told reporters after their first practice of the week they were "taking it a day at a time" with Donald.

"Just taking it a day at a time," McVay said. "I wouldn't want to say anything of that nature yet, but I think the back's a little bit sore. And he's as tough as it gets, and so I'll continue to have updates as the week goes."

The Rams have been careful not to put too much on Donald's plate early in the season as he works his way back into football shape after being retired for two years.

After sitting out Week 1 with the Rams in Australia, Donald made his season debut in Week 2. He has played a total of 68 snaps in two games, which is 54.4 percent of their defensive snaps during that period.

The Rams defense has already been playing shorthanded with Myles Garrett recovering from arthroscopic knee surgery. He is currently on injured reserve and could be out through Week 8.

Los Angeles' three sacks through three games are tied with the Eagles for 28th in the NFL.

Tyler Davis figures to get more reps against Philadelphia with Donald out. The third-year defensive lineman has eight combined tackles in three games this season.

There is good injury news for the Rams on offense with Puka Nacua expected to play Sunday after missing the last two games with a hip injury. Philadelphia could be without DeVonta Smith due to a hamstring injury.

The Rams, who entered the season as strong favorites to win the Super Bowl, have lost two of their first three games. Kickoff between the Rams and Eagles from Lincoln Financial Field is at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.

articles.title: Vikings WR Justin Jefferson ruled out with ankle sprain for Week 4 game vs. Dolphins
articles.summary: Jefferson suffered the injury on the first drive of Minnesota's Week 3 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
articles.body:
While the Minnesota Vikings have had a revolving door at quarterback of late, star wide receiver Justin Jefferson has mostly been a constant for their offense since he was drafted 22nd overall out of LSU in 2020.

The four-time All-Pro played in every Vikings regular-season game in five of his first six full seasons in the NFL.

Jefferson's availability was jeopardized during a 23-16 road win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last week, when he suffered a left ankle sprain on the game's first drive .

Although the 27-year-old wideout avoided a long-term injury, according to head coach Kevin O'Connell, he was ruled out for Sunday's home game versus the rebuilding Miami Dolphins .

Jefferson will miss his first game since 2023. That season, he was sidelined for seven straight outings with a hamstring injury .

Despite being out the majority of the Vikings' Week 3 victory against the Bucs, Jefferson still leads the team with 179 receiving yards. He's amassed that yardage on 13 receptions, two of which have resulted in touchdowns.

Jefferson is in pursuit of his seventh consecutive 1,000-yard receiving campaign. In 2022, he posted a league-leading 128 catches and an NFL-best 1,809 receiving yards. He earned NFL Offensive Player of the Year honors for his prolific efforts.

The Vikings are hoping their 2026 QB1, Kyler Murray, will maximize Jefferson's skill set. Because of the concussion Murray sustained early in the season opener and Jefferson's ankle issue, those two have hardly been on the field together so far.

They teased their rapport last week in Tampa Bay, however. Jefferson hauled in a 22-yard grab on the first play from scrimmage. The play he got hurt on saw him take a screen pass 10 yards to set up a 54-yard Will Reichard field goal.

In Jefferson's absence, Murray turned in an uneven performance, albeit with some promising throws to fourth-year wideout Jordan Addison. They hooked up for a 41-yard score in the second quarter.

Fortunately for the 3-0 Vikings, they're going up against a Dolphins secondary that's struggled mightily through three weeks. No team is giving up more net yards per pass attempt (9.1) than Miami this season .

Minnesota will take on the Saints in New Orleans in Week 5 before a Week 6 bye.

articles.title: Rams WR Puka Nacua (hip) will return to play against Eagles in Week 4
articles.summary: Nacua has not played since LA's Week 1 loss in Australia to the 49ers.
articles.body:
Puka Nacua will be back for the Los Angeles Rams in Week 4 as the team faces the Philadelphia Eagles, head coach Sean McVay announced on Friday.

McVay said Nacua "looked sharp" during Thursday's practice and that the team will likely have him on a snap count.

The wide receiver has missed the last two games while dealing with a hip/groin issue. He returned to practice on Wednesday, and while he was listed as a limited participant on Thursday, Nacua said it was a full day of work for him.

"It's exciting," Nacua said. "That's my safe space out there, and to be out there with the guys, I think that's been the most important thing, feeling that camaraderie and then also the ability to put my foot in the ground."

Nacua has not played since the Rams' Week 1 defeat to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia where he caught five passes for 74 yards.

How eager is he to get back on the field against the Eagles?

"I can't think of anything else but smiling," Nacua said.

Before Week 3, McVay told ESPN Los Angeles that Nacua was " not making great progress " in his recovery. That sounded alarm bells, but he added the injury is not a long-term concern and the team was just being cautious. The expectation was for the NFL's receptions leader last season to come back for the Eagles game.

What exactly does it mean to suspend the owner?

"Genuine question, how does an owner being suspended punish them?" Franklin wrote .

Fans certainly noticed the financial math once Friday's punishment became official.

"$500,140 for a Wheat Hill Mobile Home prostitute. Woof, Jed York," Jeff Mueller, a Doctor of Physical Therapy, shared on X.

The league has suspended owners before. The late Indianapolis Colts owner Jim Irsay received the same six-game suspension and $500,000 fine in 2014 after pleading guilty to impaired driving.

York accepted the NFL's punishment and apologized Friday, calling his actions an "inexcusable mistake" while saying he needs to earn back trust.

His full statement read: "Today, the NFL concluded its review, and I accept its decision in full. To my family, to the players, coaches, and employees of the San Francisco 49ers, to our fans and partners, I am deeply sorry. This was an inexcusable mistake and I take full responsibility. What I did does not reflect my values or the man I strive to be for my family.

"While I fell short of the model I want to set for my sons, I now hope to show them the importance of owning up to one's failures, and that even our worst moments teach us to be better. Leading the 49ers is a privilege, and one I don't take lightly. Your trust will have to be earned back over time, and I look forward to that work ahead."

While the league handed down a six-game suspension and a half-million-dollar fine, fans were still unsure how an owner's suspension affects a team.

articles.title: Aaron Donald injury update has Rams in tough spot against Eagles
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams will be without one of their key defensive figures when they take on the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams will be without one of their key defenders in Sunday's NFC heavyweight battle with the Philadelphia Eagles .

Defensive tackle Aaron Donald has been ruled out due to a back injury, coach Sean McVay announced on Friday, Oct. 2.

Donald, the three-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year who came out of retirement in late August to rejoin his former team, sat out practice Wednesday and Thursday with back soreness.

"(Donald)'s as tough as it gets. Just not feeling good enough," McVay said, according to the Los Angeles Times' Gary Klein . "He would do it and he could probably go be productive, but part of our job is to protect these tough dudes like him from themselves."

After sitting out the season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia, Donald has four tackles in two games and has yet to record a sack.

Cornerback Jaylen Watson (shoulder) and tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle) were also ruled out, but wide receiver Puka Nacua was cleared to play after missing the last two games with a hip and groin issue.

The Rams are trying to avoid falling in a 1-3 hole against the Eagles, to whom they've lost their last four contests.

articles.title: What happened to Cardinals' creative defense? And will it return?
articles.summary: The Arizona Cardinals defense was once characterized by its creative blitz and coverage schemes. But over the past two years, that has gone away.
articles.body:
Remember the Arizona Cardinals defense, just two years ago? The Cardinals entered the season low on expectations, with few blue-chip talents. It was difficult to see where high-end production would come from. And yet, they finished 15th in scoring, outpacing all expectations.

They did it by disorienting the opponent at every turn. Their defense was weird, in the best way possible. Up front, they relied on complex pressure schemes, making it difficult for offenses to know who was rushing the passer and who was dropping into coverage. In the secondary, they rotated into new looks when the ball was snapped, changing the quarterback's picture as he readied to throw.

That spring, defensive coordinator Nick Rallis was widely viewed as one of the sport's emerging young playcallers. Mike McDaniel highlighted him, unprompted, as an underrated coach, defined by his "non-traditional approach." George Kittle described it as a "very different defense than anything I've really experienced in the NFL."

But over the past two years, some of what made the Cardinals unique has disappeared. They bring less pressure, with fewer disguises. Some of the funky schematics, with the way Rallis deploys his defensive backs, have remained. It's pared down, though, from what it once was.

Arizona Cardinals' Week 3 game at San Francisco 49ers in photos

Last year, that felt understandable. With the additions of Josh Sweat and Calais Campbell up front, they didn't have to do as much to manufacture pressure. To some extent, Will Johnson had that effect on the secondary.

And through October, the Cardinals were once again a top-half defense. But after being battered by injuries, they were horrendous down the stretch. It's difficult to be creative with three new players in the lineup each week.

This year, though, the trend of Arizona's diminished creativity has only continued.

Here is how their usage of different schematic tendencies has changed over the past three seasons, per Fantasy Points Data. Blitz rate measures sending an extra pass rusher; disguise rate measures changing the secondary's shape after the snap; stunt rate measures swapping rush lanes for two or more defensive linemen.

Blitz rate: 33.8% (4), 23.3% (27), 23.3% (24)

Disguise rate: 34.9% (11), 36.7% (10), 20.0% (30)

Stunt rate: 23.3% (11), 24.0% (20), 17.8% (29)

In all three areas, the trend is clear: The Cardinals have become less creative. Even Rob Fredrickson, the former Cardinals linebacker and current radio analyst, acknowledged the difference on social media this week.

"Hey Nick, blitz Mack (Wilson) and Budda (Baker)," Fredrickson wrote. "They excel going forward.. struggle in coverage. Put Mack on the edge and bring in Cody Simon. Give the DL stunts to help them penetrate. Let's see what our DBs can do in Man"

Now, there is more nuance here than simply looking at the big picture numbers. Posed this week with a question about the Cardinals' lack of blitzes, Rallis pointed out a component of how those are measured.

Often — as is the case above — a blitz is charted as any time an extra pass rusher joins the rush. Sometimes, that can come with a dropping defensive lineman, meaning you're still rushing with four players.

Indeed, the Cardinals are rushing with five or more players at effectively the same rate as in 2024. The real change is in how their four-man rushes look. Whereas those rushes were once unpredictable — anyone could rush the passer from anywhere — they are now much more static.

"You get good at what you rep," Rallis said. "So people that major in those, I see those very effective still across the league. And if you're not majoring in it, it's probably not as effective for you."

So, why do the Cardinals no longer "major" in those looks?

"A big thing with simulateds is just, what's your personnel?" Rallis said. "And how well can those guys beat running backs? And can you find ways, within your simulateds, to get them on running backs?"

Two years ago, the Cardinals blitzed their linebackers like crazy. Wilson rushed the quarterback 9.9 times per game. Kyzir White was at 6.3. It worked because White was the defensive signal caller, patrolling the second level when Wilson blitzed, an area in which he excels.

This season, Wilson has rushed just seven times in three games. Jack Gibbens has rushed nine times in three games. That's partly because Wilson is now the signal caller, relied upon in the role that White once filled. And Gibbens is not as explosive off the edge as a pass rusher.

"Yeah, I miss blitzing, obviously," Wilson said recently. "But at the end of the day, we play whatever coach calls, and we believe in the plan he puts in every week."

If this is what the Cardinals defense does best, why did they not build around that philosophy? Since general manager Monti Ossenfort arrived, they've addressed their linebacker spots with cheap free agents and Day 3 draft picks. How could Wilson's role be different if the Cardinals paired him with a high-end coverage linebacker?

The Cardinals' player-acquisition strategy also helps explain another strange defensive trend.

So far this season, they've played base defense (looks with just four defensive backs) on 56.5% of snaps, the second-most in the NFL. Two years ago, that number was at 23.0%, the 21st most.

"We've played three teams that have very similar philosophies," head coach Mike LaFleur said. "… So just the ability to take some air out of some of the coverages that can happen in those (single linebacker) packages."

Essentially, the Cardinals have faced teams that prefer to deploy an extra running back or tight end. So to fill potential gaps in the run game, they've responded with an extra linebacker on the field.

That's a risk they might not need to take if they had more game-altering presences along the defensive line. But that group lacks players who can change the proverbial math in the run game, single-handedly filling two gaps.

And the Cardinals are paying the price. In those base packages, they're allowing 10.8 yards per pass attempt, the fifth-worst mark in the league.

Now, this is one element of the Cardinals' early-season defensive philosophy that could soon change.

"That, just by nature of the teams we were playing, feels like it's a little bit of a higher number," Rallis said.

As for Rallis' old blitzing tendencies, those might not be coming back. He denied that there has been a "philosophical change across the board," so maybe there's a chance.

"It's a game-by-game basis," Rallis said. "And then even into the flow of the game, how things are going. … There's always a time for it. And sometimes there's a time to just four-man rush and cover. And sometimes there's a healthy blend."

The challenge is finding that blend. For three weeks, it has evaded the Cardinals.

articles.title: Tony Romo Breaks Silence After Parting Ways with CBS After 9-Year Run as an NFL Analyst
articles.summary: The retired NFL quarterback was arrested for OWI (operating a vehicle while intoxicated) in Wisconsin in July
articles.body:
The former CBS Sports analyst offered a statement after parting ways with the network on Friday, Oct. 2

Romo, 46, was arrested for OWI (operating a vehicle while intoxicated) in Wisconsin in July

Tony Romo is breaking his silence after he and CBS parted ways on Friday, Oct. 2, following his OWI (operating a vehicle while intoxicated) arrest in July.

"I'm proud of what I accomplished at CBS Sports over the last nine years," Romo, 46, said in a statement , according to ESPN. "I approached my role as a game analyst the way I've approached everything in my life — with a desire to win and be the best that I can be."

He continued, "I'm going to use this time to take a break, something I've never done before, and focus on my health and my family before moving on to my next opportunity. I am grateful for my time with CBS Sports and for the continued support of my family and friends, as well as the NFL community and fans."

On Friday, the network announced that it had "mutually agreed to part ways" with the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback, who had been put on indefinite leave in the days after his July 23 arrest in Milwaukee on suspicion of operating a vehicle while intoxicated.

He initially joined the network in 2017 after retiring from the NFL.

"CBS Sports and Tony Romo have mutually agreed to part ways. We thank Tony for his contributions over the past nine years and wish him the best moving forward," the statement said.

CBS added that JJ Watt , who was elevated to Romo's role in the analyst's absence, will "continue to partner" with Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson on its lead NFL announcing team.

The retired Dallas Cowboys star and elite amateur golfer, who was in his home state of Wisconsin for a tournament when he was pulled over along Interstate 43, was given a field sobriety test at the time of his arrest. Authorities noted he performed poorly, and bodycam footage from the scene indicated that he refused a breathalyzer test .

In August, Romo received three new citations related to the arrest: first-offense operating while intoxicated , unsafe passing on the right side and possessing open intoxicants in his vehicle , per online court records.

Days later, he pleaded no contest and had his driving privileges revoked for six months.

Romo was also ordered to have an ignition interlock device installed on any vehicle he owned, attend and complete an alcohol assessment program, and pay a $784 fine.

In a statement on Instagram, Romo said he accepted the charges against him.

"Multiple back surgeries ended my career earlier than I expected and left me with constant, debilitating pain. That pain led to a dependence on pain medication, and my efforts to get off those medications led to an over-reliance on alcohol," he wrote in a Sept. 1 post.

Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE's free sports newsletter — sign up now!

Romo added that the last month had been "difficult," but forced him to "confront and own my mistakes fully—to the Lord, to myself, to my family, and now to the public."

During this time, Romo said he would work "closely with a team of doctors to address my health and make the necessary changes."

The father of three made his first public appearance since his arrest this week in Oklahoma, where he competed in the pre-qualifying stage of the PGA Tour Q-School at The Club at Forest Ridge in Broken Arrow, according to Tulsa's News on 6 .

articles.title: Young Dolphins secondary has one less worry with Justin Jefferson out
articles.summary: Minnesota Vikings star receiver Justin Jefferson was ruled out with an ankle injury for their Week 4 game vs the Miami Dolphins.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings will be without their No. 1 receiver when they face the Miami Dolphins this week. The team ruled star wide receiver Justin Jefferson out for their Week 4 game with an ankle injury.

Jefferson injured the ankle in the first half of the Vikings' 23-16 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last week. He was ruled out for the rest of the game at halftime after making two catches for 32 yards.

The two-time All-Pro and four-time Pro Bowler has played every game of the past two seasons and has put up 1,000 yards in each of his first six NFL seasons. His absence will be a major setback for the Vikings, who enter the home game Oct. 4 against the winless Dolphins as one of five 3-0 teams.

Dolphins big underdogs against Chiefs at Hard Rock Stadium

Fielding one of the youngest secondaries in the NFL, Miami has allowed the fourth-highest passer rating in the league. Opposing quarterbacks have completed 80.3% of their passes against the Dolphins, the worst in the NFL.

Minnesota will look to Jordan Addison to be Kyler Murray's top receiving option in Jefferson's stead. The former USC star has 111 yards this season, second on the team to Jefferson's 179. Second on the team in receptions is tight end T.J. Hockenson, who has nine catches for 76 yards. Both have one TD this year.

"The thing with their team is I got a lot of respect for the other receivers," Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said. "I was in that division for two years. I think Addison is one of the most underrated and undertalked-about wide receivers in the league, and sometimes that happens when you have one of the top players in the league. I think Addison's really good."

The Dolphins vs. Vikings matchup will now be without both of the teams' biggest stars after Miami running back De'Von Achane was lost for the season with a torn ACL.

articles.title: NFL Puts Pressure on Illinois in Latest Bears Stadium Talks
articles.summary: Roger Goodell and JB Pritzker had their first face-to-face meeting.
articles.body:
The NFL's message to Illinois leaders is very clear: it's essentially now or never on a stadium deal to possibly keep the Bears in the state.

League commissioner Roger Goodell met Thursday in Chicago with state Gov. JB Pritzker, along with several other lawmakers including state House Speaker Emanuel "Chris" Welch and state Rep. Kam Buckner, a key figure on prior stadium negotiations with the Bears.

The session marked the first face-to-face meeting between Goodell and Pritzker about the proposed stadium. Throughout the multiyear facility saga that has enveloped the franchise, though, the two have been in regular contact, particularly over the last year. In the latest session, the NFL made it clear that time was of the essence if the Bears are to stay in Illinois.

"Timely action is essential as the Bears work to find a long-term stadium solution for the club and their fans," the NFL said in a statement.

The meeting happened as the Bears continued to advance deliberations on a potential, and perhaps likely, move to Hammond, Indiana. Already, state leaders there have approved a funding package for a new stadium , and as recently as August, Bears president Kevin Warren said that Hammond was the team's "sole focus" on the stadium front.

That statement followed a vote by the team's board of directors to advance the Hammond project , a move that in part responded to the Illinois spring legislative session ending without any action on the Bears .

"Hope is not a strategy," Bears chairman George McCaskey said before the season regarding Illinois, and seemingly non-existent efforts then to resurrect a legislative response there.

Notably, Thursday's meeting did not include McCaskey and Warren, who lead the franchise and have been front and center on the stadium deliberations, but have occasionally rankled Illinois leaders. Instead, the session included billionaire businessman Pat Ryan, who has a sizable minority Bears stake. Ryan has deep connections across the Chicago area, and he also was the key benefactor in Northwestern's $875 million Ryan Field, opening Friday.

"The Governor and General Assembly leadership were glad to participate in a productive meeting focused on keeping the Bears in Illinois and protecting taxpayers," Pritzker's office said in a statement.

Getting an Illinois stadium bill for the Bears revived will require scheduling something during the upcoming fall veto session, which runs for six combined days during late November and early December. As a result, it will require a heavy lift for Illinois leaders to coalesce the type of political consensus that was lacking in the spring.

It also means that Chicago-area legislators will need to abandon any hope of a downtown stadium option for the Bears, as no viable location currently exists. A continued search for one by some leaders, including Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson, complicated the prior political efforts.

The Bears had been seeking property tax certainty regarding a potential project on team-owned land in Arlington Heights, Illinois, as well as infrastructure support.

Meanwhile, the team continues to work through due diligence on two potential stadium sites in Hammond. That city's mayor, Thomas McDermott Jr., remains confident of closing a deal with the Bears, and said he was informed in advance of the NFL's meeting with the Illinois leaders.

"The reason the Bears wanted me to know is they want me to know how serious they are about Hammond and how the NFL has steps that they have to go through to close the door on Illinois as well," McDermott said in a livestream on the city's Facebook page. "I trust that we are in the lead and that we're going to get this deal done."

articles.title: What has Kenneth Walker III brought to Kansas City Chiefs’ offense?
articles.summary: 5 questions with the enemy ahead of the battle for first place
articles.body:
While the Las Vegas Raiders and Kansas City Chiefs have a historic rivalry, the two teams haven't met with first place in the AFC West on the line in about a decade (Dec. 8, 2016). Technically, Las Vegas has never been involved in this type of matchup with Kansas City since the Raiders were still in Oakland back then.

It's still early in the season, but the Week 4 contest between the Raiders and Chiefs is one of the biggest regular-season games the Silver and Black have played in a long time. To preview the huge matchup, Silver and Black Pride reached out to our frienemies at Arrowhead Pride, and Maurice Elston was kind enough to answer a few questions about Kansas City for Raider Nation.

Q: Kenneth Walker III was the Chiefs' big offseason addition and hasn't disappointed, with 442 yards from scrimmage and four total touchdowns in the first three games. How has he revitalized Kansas City's offense?

A: The easiest way to explain Walker's impact is that Patrick Mahomes has never had a 1,000-yard rusher during his career as the Chiefs' starting quarterback. Kareem Hunt rushed for 824 yards in 11 games during Mahomes' first season as the starter before being released, but every Chiefs backfield since then has consisted primarily of serviceable players rather than a dynamic, home-run threat like Walker.

Walker has helped Kansas City operate from under center and lean more heavily on play action. Against Miami, Mahomes completed 11 of 12 play-action passes for 183 yards. That is a dimension we have not consistently seen from this offense in recent years, when it relied more heavily on shotgun formations and RPOs.

Walker's success also changes how defenses must prepare for Kansas City. In previous seasons, opponents could concentrate on limiting Mahomes and preventing explosive passing plays. Now, if a defense sits back in coverage with light boxes, Kansas City can hand the ball to Walker. His presence has restored balance and forced opponents to defend every part of the offense.

Q: What's going on with expected starting left tackle Josh Simmons? Is there any timeline for his return? What can you tell us about Fernando Mendoza's college teammate, Kahlil Benson, who has been filling in for Simmons?

A: The Chiefs have been extremely vague about Josh Simmons' back injury. Andy Reid has described him as week-to-week but has not provided a firm timetable, recently telling reporters that he would let them know when Simmons was ready to return. I do not believe anyone outside the organization can confidently offer more than assumptions right now.

One of my high school coaches always said that you cannot worry about who is not on the field—you have to focus on who is. Right now, that player is Kahlil Benson, an undrafted rookie who played with Fernando Mendoza at Indiana.

Benson has experienced some expected challenges while transitioning from primarily playing on the right side to starting at left tackle in the NFL. However, nobody should be disappointed with his overall performance. Through three games, he has allowed six pressures and two quarterback hits but no sacks. He has been particularly effective as a run blocker, earning a 74.7 run-blocking grade from Pro Football Focus .

His pass protection has been serviceable, and sometimes that is exactly what an offense needs from a rookie thrown into this situation. He certainly has not hurt the offense. Sunday's matchup with Maxx Crosby will easily be one of the most difficult tests he has faced.

Q: It's only been three games, but Travis Kelce has his highest yards per game ( 77.0 ) since 2022 and looks much more like his old self so far this season. Besides marrying one of the biggest celebrities in the world over the summer, what's been different for Kelce compared to the last three or four years?

A: The improved running and play-action games have helped Kelce as much as anyone. He remains an excellent route runner who understands how to find the soft spots in a defense. Now, linebackers and safeties must respect Walker and the running game before dropping into coverage.

Kansas City has used play action on 36% of its passing plays, the highest rate in the league. That has helped create open space for Kelce, who has 14 catches for 231 yards and is averaging 16.5 yards per reception through three games.

Kelce also deserves personal credit. He appears to be in some of the best shape we have seen him in over the past few seasons, and he is playing with a fire that seemed to be missing at times during the last couple of years. I believe he will return to the 1,000-yard mark this season and remind everyone why he is still one of the NFL's best tight ends—and, in my opinion, the greatest tight end of all time.

Q: Kansas City made some significant changes in the secondary this offseason, most notably trading away All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie and drafting Mansoor Delane as McDuffie's replacement. How have the rookie and the rest of the defensive backfield looked so far?

A: Delane could not have scripted a much better beginning to his career. He intercepted the first NFL pass thrown in his direction against Denver, although he injured his shoulder on the play. He missed the remainder of that game and dressed against Indianapolis only as an emergency option.

His first complete game came against Miami, and he showed why the Chiefs selected him sixth overall. Delane recorded 10 tackles, including a tackle for loss, and broke up a fourth-down pass. He was targeted seven times and allowed five completions, but those catches produced only 24 yards. His tackling, physicality and ability to limit yards after the catch were impressive.

Opposite Delane, Nohl Williams has been excellent. I believe the Chiefs' belief in Williams—and what they saw from him as a rookie—helped give them the confidence to trade McDuffie. Delane and Williams already look capable of becoming a strong young outside-cornerback combination.

The rest of the secondary has been more inconsistent. L'Jarius Sneed has allowed an 80% completion rate when targeted, although he continues to contribute in other ways. Against Miami, he generated five pressures as a blitzer and forced a turnover. The safeties had a difficult game against the Dolphins, with Alohi Gilman taking some poor angles and Jaden Hicks not playing the ball as well as we are accustomed to seeing.

Chamarri Conner's eventual return from his knee injury should help. It will also give us our first real opportunity to see him consistently play his natural safety position rather than primarily working in the slot. This is a young secondary, but I expect it to improve as the season progresses.

Q: When it comes to the Chiefs' defensive line, Raider Nation knows Chris Jones and George Karlaftis pretty well at this point. But is there a d-lineman or two who is new or flying under the radar and could make a major impact on Sunday?

A: R Mason Thomas is the first player who comes to mind. The rookie has natural pass-rushing ability, gets off the ball quickly and already has his first NFL sack. His role is also expanding. He played 41 defensive snaps against Miami, which was 10 more than starter Felix Anudike-Uzomah.

Peter Woods is another rookie whose role continues to grow. He played 35 snaps against Miami, five more than starting defensive tackle Khyiris Tonga. Woods has not produced many traditional pass-rushing statistics yet, but he is becoming a bigger part of the defensive-line rotation every week.

The player I would watch most closely Sunday, however, is Anudike-Uzomah.

He is in a contract year after the Chiefs declined his fifth-year option, and he has quietly played solid football. The Chiefs' overall pass rush has not been as productive as expected, but some of that can be attributed to Chris Jones playing through a calf injury. Once Jones returns to full strength and starts dominating the interior again, it should create more one-on-one opportunities for Anudike-Uzomah, Thomas and the other edge rushers.

articles.title: NFL hands down Jed York decision that mirrors past owner punishment
articles.summary: The NFL closed its review of San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York on Friday. The decision came 39 days after a league spokesperson said his arrest in Ohio woul...
articles.body:
The NFL closed its review of San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York on Friday. The decision came 39 days after a league spokesperson said his arrest in Ohio would be reviewed under the Personal Conduct Policy.

Police arrested York on Aug. 23 at a mobile home park in East Palestine, Ohio, during a sting by the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force. Police said he responded to an undercover online prostitution advertisement and attempted to pay $160 for sex. Prosecutors amended an initial charge of engaging in prostitution. The next day, York pleaded no contest to misdemeanor counts of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools, a plea that neither admits guilt nor contests the allegations.

He received a one-day jail sentence with credit for time served. He also paid $1,150 in fines and forfeited the $160 seized in the sting.

On Friday, the league suspended York for six regular-season games and fined him $500,000.

Those terms match exactly what the NFL gave Indianapolis Colts owner Jim Irsay in 2014, after Irsay pleaded guilty to a misdemeanor impaired-driving charge. Irsay's $500,000 fine was the maximum permitted under league rules at the time. His suspension barred him from the team facility, practices, games and league meetings, and from media interviews and social media about team or league matters.

How York's penalty compares with the policy's standard for owners

The policy itself sets a higher bar for people in York's position. It states that "ownership and club or league management have traditionally been held to a higher standard and will be subject to more significant discipline when violations of the Policy occur."

Twelve years after Irsay, the league met that standard by repeating his penalty to the game and to the dollar.

Commissioner Roger Goodell had kept his public comments brief while the review played out.

"It's being reviewed under the personal conduct policy," Goodell said on Aug. 26 at the owners' meetings in Atlanta. "We'll do that and when there's something to be reported we'll talk."

York's family has been through this before. His uncle, former 49ers owner Eddie DeBartolo Jr., was suspended for the 1999 season and fined $1 million after pleading guilty to failing to report a felony tied to a Louisiana riverboat gambling license. Control of the team passed to his sister, Denise DeBartolo York, who is Jed York's mother.

The younger York had already kept his distance from the 49ers this season. He traveled to Australia for the Week 1 game against the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne but did not attend it. He also stayed away from the Sept. 20 home opener against the Miami Dolphins.

articles.title: Houston Texans face uncomfortable truth after ex-linemen shine elsewhere
articles.summary: Houston poured draft capital and money into its offensive line, only to watch two traded blockers excel for other teams.
articles.body:
For Houston Texans fans, watching Thursday Night Football's matchup between the Cleveland Browns and the Pittsburgh Steelers might've been a triggering experience.

Former Texans offensive lineman Tytus Howard, who was unceremoniously traded to the Browns for just a fifth-round pick, was lined up across from Steelers star pass rusher T.J. Watt all night. Howard, who spent seven seasons with the Texans, was a proficient blocker and protector against the future Hall of Fame defender.

Howard's play helped stabilize the Browns' offensive line and, more importantly, stifle the Steelers.

Let's be clear: Howard's stellar play on Thursday doesn't necessarily mean the Texans let go of an all-world tackle for pennies. Over eight seasons, Howard has proven he's a replacement-level offensive lineman.

However, when the Texans agreed to a trade with the Detroit Lions, receiving running back David Montgomery in exchange for offensive lineman Juice Scruggs, many in Houston felt they fleeced Detroit.

Scruggs, pushed into starting duty at center due to injuries, has thrived. According to Pro Football Focus, Scruggs has graded out as the NFL's fourth-best center (71.5) through three games. Moreover, Scruggs has been dominant as a run blocker, grading out as the league's second-best center (78.7) in that phase of the game.

For Texans fans, it must be difficult to reconcile how well former offensive linemen are now performing elsewhere. Meanwhile, Pro Football Focus currently grades the Texans' offensive line No. 30 out of 32 teams in the NFL.

The Texans have thrown a lot of resources at fixing arguably the most problem-plagued unit in franchise history this offseason. Texans general manager Nick Caserio used a first-round pick to draft interior lineman Keylan Rutledge. Caserio also signed veteran free agents Evan Brown and Wyatt Teller to bolster the unit.

So far, the Texans are 0-3, while quarterback C.J. Stroud was tied for second-most sacks taken after three weeks. Moreover, the Texans' rushing attack has averaged a meager 84.7 yards per game, ranking 30th out of 32 teams.

"We're still making gains. We're gonna go out there and just execute better from a down-to-down basis. And it starts with me, we're all in this together," Texans offensive line coach Cole Popovich said to KPRC's Aaron Wilson on Thursday . "We'll keep coaching it, the players will keep coming along, keep getting it, and we'll just keep improving as we go."

The Texans are officially at a breaking point yet again, with an offensive line unable to be difference-makers for a team that seemed destined for title contention this season. With the rival Dallas Cowboys coming into town, they bring one of the league's worst defenses, currently ranked No. 23 by PFF.

Another poor performance will raise tough questions for everyone involved in the offense, from the quarterback and coordinators to assistant coaches and even the general manager. Just being average would likely do wonders. Because 0-4 might mean thinking more about a high draft pick in 2027 than hosting a playoff game or two.

articles.title: NFL finally punishes Jed York: 49ers owner gets $500K fine, 6-game suspension
articles.summary: The NFL announced York's punishment late Friday morning.
articles.body:
The NFL has officially suspended Jed York in the league's first punishment of a notable team owner in over four years.

York, the San Francisco 49ers' principal owner, will serve a six-game suspension for his Aug. 23 arrest in Ohio, where he was caught up in a local online prostitution sting . York also received a $500,000 fine. In the NFL's statement, the league said York's suspension will count the first three games of the 49ers' season, since he stayed away from the team during that time. York can return to team duties starting Oct. 20.

In a statement sent out to 49ers and NFL reporters, York said: "Today, the NFL conducted its review, and I accept its decision in full. To my family, to the players, coaches, and employees of the San Francisco 49ers, to our fans and partners, I am deeply sorry. This was an inexcusable mistake and I take full responsibility. What I did does not reflect my values or the man I strive to be for my family. While I fell short of the model I want to set for my sons, I now hope to show them the importance of owning up to one's failures, and that even our worst moments teach us to be better. Leading the 49ers is a privilege, and one I don't take lightly. Your trust will have to be earned back over time, and I look forward to that work ahead."

The last time the NFL handed a majority owner this kind of punishment was against the Miami Dolphins' Stephen Ross, who was suspended for approximately 11 weeks, from Aug. 2 to Oct. 17, 2022, for breaking league anti-tampering rules. However, the NFL went much further than a suspension, as it also fined Ross $1.5 million and took away two draft picks: a 2023 first-rounder and a 2024 third-rounder. The last time an owner was punished by the NFL for non-football conduct came in 2014 , when the league suspended former Indianapolis Colts owner Jim Irsay for six games in the wake of a DUI arrest.

It's worth noting that while the NFL might have had an apt comparison with Patriots owner Robert Kraft, who was charged with two counts of first-degree solicitation after he allegedly visited a Florida massage parlor for sex acts, the charges against Kraft were later dropped . An appeals court ruled video evidence of the owner - which a judge later ruled was unlawfully obtained - couldn't be used in the case, and Kraft was never punished by the NFL. York, meanwhile, was arrested and booked and pleaded no contest to his charges all within a whirlwind 24 hours, leading to $1,150 in fines and this punishment from the league.

The 49ers have been by all accounts preparing for some version of this announced outcome for a while now. General manager John Lynch told San Francisco Standard columnist Tim Kawakami before the season that he and head coach Kyle Shanahan were already holding regularly scheduled meetings with York while he was in Ohio, and the topic of what would happen in York's absence has already come up.

"Let's have conversations beforehand, so that we know exactly where his wishes are," Lynch said on a podcast published Sept. 2. "And you can't do that for everything, because issues come up, like trade deadline. You don't know until you know. There's so many factors that go into that, but we will be prepared for everything, because we've put in the work, we've put in the communication beforehand."

York has reportedly not attended any 49ers games so far this season, though one questionable report from ESPN's Adam Schefter said he flew out to Australia even though he didn't attend the game. The team also repeatedly emphasized that York's arrest would have no effect on the on-field side of things within the organization. So far, the team has appeared prepared as ever, starting the season off 3-0.

articles.title: Cowboys Weren't Only Team That Called Steelers About Joey Porter Jr.
articles.summary: Detroit made a serious push for Joey Porter Jr. before the Steelers ultimately sent the cornerback to Dallas.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys weren't the only team interested in Joey Porter Jr. before the Pittsburgh Steelers traded the cornerback this week.

The Detroit Lions also made a push for Porter, with head coach Dan Campbell confirming Friday that Detroit was heavily involved in trade discussions.

"We were very much in on him," Campbell told reporters .

Pittsburgh ultimately sent Porter to Dallas in exchange for a 2028 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick.

The Steelers selected Porter early in the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft. He started 41 of the 47 regular-season games he played in Pittsburgh, finishing his three seasons with 165 tackles, 31 passes defended and three interceptions.

Detroit's interest in Porter comes as the Lions look to stabilize their cornerback room.

Now, Porter will begin the next chapter of his career with the Cowboys, while Pittsburgh moves forward with the draft capital it received in the trade.

articles.title: How Rays' 2025 trade with Orioles could lead to World Series title
articles.summary: This trade has turned out splendidly for the Rays.
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Rays are looking to win the organization's first World Series championship.

Tampa Bay made the Fall Classic in 2008 but fell short against the Philadelphia Phillies .

First, they'll match up with the New York Yankees in the ALDS.

A pivotal part of a championship squad is the back end of a bullpen, specifically the closer.

Right-hander Bryan Baker has emerged as one of the best in the business, posting a 1.44 ERA with 41 saves in 65 appearances in 2026.

Bleacher Report's Joel Reuter wrote that Baker is Tampa Bay's "biggest surprise" of the season.

"After declining their club option on Pete Fairbanks last winter, the Rays entered the season without a set closer.

"By season's end, Baker was tied for the MLB lead with 41 saves, using a lethal fastball-changeup combination to turn in a season that should earn him Mariano Rivera AL Reliever of the Year honors. The 31-year-old was acquired from the Orioles midway through the 2025 season," Reuter added.

In return for Baker, the Orioles received a Competitive Balance A Round Draft pick, which turned into outfielder Slater de Brun.

de Brun is still a few years away from making an impact in the Majors, while Baker is arguably a top-five closer in baseball.

The NFL has fined San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York $500,000 and suspended him for six regular-season games for violating the league's personal conduct policy.

"During the time the league's investigation has been proceeding, York has stayed away from the 49ers' first three regular-season games, as well as from NFL league meetings," the league said in a statement on Friday, via NFL Network's Mike Garafolo .

"Those three missed games are counted toward his suspension, and he may return on Tuesday, Oct. 20."

That return coincides with Week 7 of the 2026 campaign, during which the currently undefeated Niners will face the Atlanta Falcons on the road on Oct. 25.

York also released a statement on Friday:

York, who reportedly filed for divorce from his wife in May , used the pseudonym "Joe" when engaging with a fake advertisement police deployed while it masqueraded as a woman, according to a Friday report from The Athletic , which cited an incident report from the Mahoning Valley Law Enforcement Task Force.

A meeting was arranged at a mobile home park in in East Palestine, Ohio.

York, a Youngstown, Ohio, native, reportedly agreed to one hour of "full service sexual activity" for $160. He was given a fake lot number in the mobile home park, identified as the Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community in ESPN's Aug. 25 report .

After York couldn't find the made-up lot number, he was stopped by police and arrested, per The Athletic's Aug. 25 report .

At first, York faced a prostitution charge that was eventually amended to disorderly conduct through a plea agreement, per ESPN . Additionally, York was charged with possession of criminal tools, a classification that can apply to a cell phone, which he used to communicate with the fictitious prostitute in the sting.

He pleaded no contest to both of those misdemeanors and was sentenced to two days in jail. Plus, York had to pay a $1,150 fine, according to The Athletic's Friday report .

Notably, New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft didn't receive a punishment from the NFL after he was accused of paying for sex with a woman at a massage parlor. However, the charges against Kraft, misdemeanor counts of soliciting prostitution, were dropped.

York was handed the same penalty — a $500,000 fine and six-game suspension — late Indianapolis Colts owner Jim Irsay dealt with after he pleaded guilty to operating a vehicle while intoxicated in 2014.

York has been in charge of the 49ers for close to two decades. In 2008, he assumed day-to-day control of the team from his parents when he was named CEO. Then, in 2024, he purchased enough equity from his family to take over as the organization's principal owner.

San Francisco has made three Super Bowl appearances under York's supervision, except the franchise hasn't won it all since the 1994 season, well before the York family took control of the Niners in 2000.
